title: Sales Associate (Part-Time), Los Angeles
description:
About ALSO.

We’re ALSO, an electric mobility company originally conceived as a part of Rivian. We’re a passionate team of builders, dreamers, doers and innovators, focused on creating entirely new (not to mention, innovative and delightful) vertically integrated, small EVs designed to meet the global mobility challenges of today and tomorrow. Our mission is to inspire everyone to ride ALSO—replacing many local car, truck and SUV miles with ones on vehicles that are more affordable, more enjoyable and 10-50x more efficient.




ALSO is looking for a Part-Time Sales Associate to support the launch and growth of our brand in/around Los Angeles. This is a field-based, customer-facing role that works closely with and reports to the Market Manager to bring ALSO to life through mobile demos, retail experiences, and community activations. You’ll be on the front lines—introducing customers to our vehicles, delivering exceptional experiences, and helping build the foundation of ALSO’s presence in Los Angeles.

This role is ideal for someone who is energetic, people-oriented, and excited to be part of an early-stage brand with room to grow.

 

What You Will Do

Customer Experience & Sales Support

 - Deliver engaging, high-quality customer experiences in both mobile and fixed retail environments.

 - Educate customers on ALSO vehicles, features, and benefits, guiding them through demo rides and early purchase consideration.

 - Support local sales goals by converting interest into qualified leads and sales.

 - Share customer feedback and insights with the Market Manager to improve execution and experiences.

Mobile Demo & Event Support

 - Assist with the setup, execution, and breakdown of mobile demo experiences and local activation events, including driving the custom Rivian EV van to/from events.

 - Safely operate and maintain the local demo fleet, ensuring vehicles are clean, charged, and customer-ready.

 - Represent ALSO at community events, pop-ups, and partner activations.

Retail Store Operations (in applicable markets, over time)

 - Support daily retail hub operations, including opening and closing procedures, merchandising, and general upkeep.

 - Deliver best-in-class customer service and demonstrate active selling skills.

 - Help create a welcoming, on-brand environment that reflects ALSO’s premium and playful ethos.

Operational Support

 - Follow operational, safety, and compliance processes as directed by the Market Manager and/or Market Coordinator.
   
   
   

What You Will Bring

 - 1+ years of experience in retail, events, sales, hospitality, brand ambassador, or customer-facing roles.

 - A positive, proactive attitude and willingness to jump in wherever needed - you actively engage in your professional development.

 - Strong interpersonal and communication skills—you enjoy talking to people, telling a compelling story, and actively selling products and services.

 - Ability to work in a dynamic, field-based environment, including weekends and events - you have a flexible work style and enjoy variety in your work schedule.

 - Interest in cycling, electric vehicles and/or innovative consumer brands - your enthusiasm for our brand is infectious!

 - Ability to work collaboratively while also taking direction and feedback well - you are a charismatic and fun team player!

 - A strong connection to, knowledge of and comfort riding a bike in Los Angeles is a plus!

 - Qualify as an authorized driver, meaning you are at least 21 years of age, have a valid U.S. driver’s license with a minimum of three (3) years of licensed driving experience, and can successfully complete a background screening and motor vehicle review - because you’ll be driving our demo van and fleet of bikes to meet customers where they like to ride!
   
   
   

This position offers an hourly pay rate of $21.00 per hour and is eligible to participate in the sales incentive program in accordance with the terms of the applicable plan. This role is expected to work approximately 20–24 hours per week. As a part-time position working fewer than 30 hours per week, this role is not eligible for company-sponsored benefits.

Why ALSO.

We’re passionate about helping the world find a better way to get there—wherever it is you’re headed.

We’re located in the heart of Silicon Valley and have brought together a world-class team from some of the biggest brands in the technology, automotive, cycling, outdoor recreation and retail spaces. 

Together we’re working hands-on to imagine, design and build an entirely new solution to a global set of transportation challenges.

The Associate Director, Oncology Market Access Marketing plays a key role in preparing for the anticipated first-line DLBCL launch while supporting the brand across current and future indications. The role gathers and synthesizes payer, provider, reimbursement, channel, and field insights to support U.S. Market Access strategy development and execute the tactical plan. It builds the evidence, resources, partnerships, and operational readiness needed to protect access and support EPKINLY adoption. Success requires close collaboration within the AbbVie–Genmab alliance to align execution, share insights, and advance joint priorities.
Primary Responsibilities
Launch Readiness and Preparedness
•  Support Market Access readiness and preparedness for the anticipated EPKINLY first-line DLBCL launch by gathering and synthesizing payer, provider, reimbursement, channel, and field insights; coordinating readiness activities; tracking milestones and risks; and executing launch tactics in partnership with cross-functional and Genmab colleagues.
•  Gather insights from field teams, analytics, research, customers, and alliance partners to inform strategy development, brand planning, launch readiness, and financial planning.
•  Develop analyses, dashboards, and scenario assessments that help evaluate access risks, opportunities, trade-offs, and tactical performance.
Tactical Planning and Execution
•  Translate the Market Access strategy into actionable tactics, timelines, milestones, and performance measures across current and future indications.
•  Lead development, approval, launch, training, pull-through, and optimization of customer and field resources addressing access, reimbursement, value, and operational barriers.
•  Manage agency and vendor partners, budget, scopes of work, and cross-functional dependencies to deliver high-quality work on time.

•  Coordinate cross-functional work with Brand, Payer and Corporate Accounts, Analytics, HEOR, Strategic Pricing, Trade, Patient Services, Medical, Legal, Regulatory, OEC, and field teams.
•  Support recurring access forums by preparing insights, tracking actions, surfacing risks, and helping resolve executional barriers or escalate areas of misalignment.
Access and Adoption
•  Execute initiatives that protect broad access and enable EPKINLY adoption across payer channels and sites of care, particularly community oncology.

•  Knowledge of medical-benefit access, Medicare fee-for-service and commercial payer dynamics, utilization management, reimbursement, buy-and-bill economics, and provider or site-of-care considerations.

•  Ability to manage multiple high-priority workstreams, ambiguity, shifting timelines, agency partners, and budgets while maintaining strong execution discipline.
Preferred Qualifications
•  Oncology, hematology, or HCP-administered product experience strongly preferred.
•  At least 3 years of U.S. Market Access experience preferred.

•  Experience with community oncology, GPOs, clinical pathways, payer and provider value communication, 340B, OPPS, ASP/WAC dynamics, or provider economics.
•  Alliance or co-commercialization experience strongly preferred, including experience coordinating shared priorities and deliverables across organizations.
•  Experience developing promotional and non-promotional resources for health care decision-makers and operational stakeholders.

description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. As Principal Data Scientist I, you are a technical leader and lead data scientist who design, build, and oversee bioinformatics platforms and data systems that streamline, integrate, and standardize scientific workflows across R&D. In this role, you will develop a deep understanding of how scientists work and what they need, then translate that into systems and data solutions with the business partner organizations they support. You will lead the development of multi-omics bioinformatics platforms and oversee the data pipelines and data operations that bring scientific data into them, managing a team of developers and bioinformaticians. You will serve as the site lead for the Cambridge satellite sites and Waltham, acting as the single point of contact to leadership and coordinating requests from site leadership to the appropriate internal teams. You will work and collaborate with teams in Neuroscience, Immunology, Quantitative Medicine and Genomics, Personalized Medicine, and Biologics and Genetic Medicine.
Responsibilities
Workflow analysis and system design . Work with scientists and business partner organizations to understand scientific workflows and requirements, then design systems that streamline, integrate, and standardize them. Ensure solutions are scalable, reproducible, and adopted by the scientists who rely on them.
Multi-omics platform leadership. Own the design and delivery of bioinformatics platforms supporting multi-omics modalities, with accountability for quality, usability, and maintainability across therapeutic areas.
Data pipelines and data operations . Oversee the pipelines and data operations that move scientific data into these systems, including ingestion, processing, validation, and monitoring. Ensures data is reliable, traceable, and fit for downstream analysis.
Team management . Manage and develop a team of software developers and bioinformaticians. Set priorities, guide and evaluate performance, and accountable for the team’s output and quality.

AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules to Late Stage Clinical.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.
Position Description:
This Senior Scientist – Solid State Characterization position will be in a technical specialty group - Physical Analytical Chemistry (PAC) withing Analytical R&D.  The PAC group is a global team of experienced and innovative scientists which utilize a diverse set of physical analytical tools to advance CMC development programs by providing insights and driving the understanding of materials, processes, and products.  Additionally, the group contributes to development and justification of control strategies and authors relevant sections of regulatory submissions across all development phases.
We are looking for a subject matter expert in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of drug substances (DS) and drug products (DP), from early form discovery through regulatory filing. The role focuses on single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), electron diffraction (3D ED/MicroED), Rietveld refinement, quantitative phase analysis (QPA), and phase-appropriate polymorph quantitation methods both in drug substance and drug products. The scientist will work closely with Molecular Profiling Drug Development, Process Chemistry, Formulation, Process Engineering, Analytical, Operations, Quality Assurance and CMC-Regulatory.
Key Responsibilities:
Support new product development with advanced methods development and validations, technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements.
Serve as technical SME in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of DS and DP; Responsible for PXRD method development for DS and DP, validation/technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements
Serve as the PXRD expert for supporting solid form screening, identification, crystallinity, and stability studies; perform indexing, Pawley/Le Bail fitting, Rietveld refinement, and structure determination from powder data.
Perform quantitative phase analysis: Quantify polymorphic and amorphous content in DS and DP using Rietveld, whole-pattern, and multivariate approaches, addressing low drug load, excipient interference, preferred orientation, and micro absorption.
Apply advanced diffraction such as VT/VH-XRPD, in situ, synchrotron, and PDF analysis to study phase transformations and poorly crystalline/amorphous materials.
Apply SCXRD and 3D ED/MicroED structure determination, including absolute configuration and crystal packing of APIs, salts, cocrystals, hydrates, and solvates; generate calculated powder patterns and CIF reports.
Conduct orthogonal solid-state characterization including X-ray diffraction, thermal analysis, moisture sorption, microscopy, spectroscopy as applicable for solid form, impurity and stability studies
Support solid form control strategies per ICH Q6A, author Module 3 sections and health authority responses, and ensure GMP and data integrity compliance.
Highly autonomous and productive in performing laboratory work, method development and troubleshoot; processing, interpreting, and visualizing data to facilitate project team decisions
Represent PAC on CMC teams, lead form-change investigations, mentor scientists, and implement new diffraction technologies.
Build strong relationships with peers and cross functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance.
Routinely demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in research or development activities and maintain a high level of productivity in the lab.
Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, controlled drug and radioactive compounds, and GxP compliance, where applicable.
Qualifications:
Bachelors, Masters, or Ph.D. in Chemistry, Material Science, Physics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field typically with minimum 10 (BS), 8 (MS), or 0 – 2 (Ph.D.) years related industry experience.
Strong technical background in solid state characterization, excellent analytical problem-solving, communication, presentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Capable of independently developing and troubleshoot analytical methods.
Extensive hands-on PXRD experience, including indexing, Rietveld refinement, QPA, and polymorph and amorphous quantitation.
Track record of developing and validating PXRD methods for DS and DP in a GMP environment, with knowledge of ICH Q2(R2), Q6A, Q14, and USP .
Expertise in small molecule SCXRD structure solution and refinement, including disorder modeling and absolute structure; and knowledge of 3D ED/MicroED approaches.
Proficiency with tools such as Olex2, SHELX, CrysAlisPro, TOPAS, Diffrac Eva and DQuant, GSAS-II, HighScore, Mercury, and the CSD.
Hands-on experience with DSC, TGA, hot-stage and polarized light microscopy, DVS, and strong data analysis and interpretation skills.
Experience with Raman/FTIR/NIR, solid-state NMR, SEM, SAXS, micro-CT, and crystal structure prediction, and particle characterization is preferred.
Experience with AI/ML and data science for automation of phase identification and Rietveld/QPA workflows, chemometrics, and Python or R scripting is preferred.
Experience with biophysical characterization tools of nanoDSC, DLS, SEC-MALS, CD, AUC, nanoDSF in peptide, LNP and biologic materials, formulations and process characterization is preferred.
Strong pharmaceutical industry experience in solid state characterization is preferred
Ability to coordinate activities and work simultaneously on multiple projects, in a global, fast-paced setting where priorities may change quickly.
High attention to detail and creative problem solving while exhibiting strong interpersonal skills and proven ability to work independently as well as part of cross functional teams
Knowledge of instrument set-up, troubleshooting, management and maintenance.
Experience extracting insights from multidimensional data sets, along with other physical analytical characterizations, and connecting to pharmaceutical materials, processes, and products
Practical knowledge of organic structure, functional groups, chemistry, and modern spectroscopic techniques as applied to small-molecule analytical analysis.

Write quality systems records including laboratory investigations, change controls, non-conformances.
Support regulatory inspections where needed.
Participate in CBPA method transfers and validations.
Support laboratory equipment preventive maintenance and the qualification of new laboratory equipment.
Authoring and review of documents such as protocols, reports, test methods, SOPs.

The External Search & AI Optimization team's mission is to make Airbnb the most visible and trusted destination wherever people search for travel, from traditional search engines to AI answer engines and assistants. Technical breadth across web frontend, backend services, and data pipelines, with the judgment to guide architecture decisions.
Experience applying machine learning or LLMs in production, and using experimentation to measure impact.

Strong communication and influence with technical and non-technical partners, including Product, Marketing, Data, Finance, and Legal.
Comfort leading through ambiguity, balancing short-term business outcomes with long-term technical and team health.

Our scope spans high-impact datasets across the organization: measuring AI adoption, usage, and cost; understanding revenue, costs, and profitability through Unit Economics; integrating non-platform data from Jira and other enterprise applications; and powering critical company metrics such as Gross Booking Value and Revenue.

We collaborate with engineering, product, analytics, finance, and business teams to turn complex requirements into dependable, reusable data assets. As a Senior Data Engineer, you will design, build, and operate datasets that shape decisions across Airbnb. Your work will help the organization measure AI adoption and spending, understand the economics of its products, and connect enterprise application data to meaningful business and operational insights.
You will own complex data engineering projects from requirements gathering and technical design through implementation, validation, and production operations. Working closely with stakeholders and engineering partners, you will build maintainable data models and pipelines that accommodate new AI tools, products, cost categories, and enterprise systems while preserving clear definitions, traceability, and reliable historical data.
Operating in an ecosystem that includes petabyte-scale datasets, you will improve correctness, freshness, performance, and cost efficiency. You will build reusable components that simplify source onboarding and reduce duplicated logic. title: Power & Hydrogen Program Manager, Power & Hydrogen Solutions, GESA
description:
An execution-focused project/program manager responsible for the hands-on coordination and completion of power capacity and hydrogen fuel cell projects across the Amazon fulfillment network. This is a delivery role with a strong bias for action: the PM owns the details, gets into the field, and drives projects from feasibility through commissioning and handover. Oversees multiple concurrent projects spanning temporary and permanent power deployment (utility upgrades, generator installations, switchgear deployments, and air permitting) as well as hydrogen fuel cell execution — including decommissioning of existing assets, launch of new hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cells per Amazon standards and processes, and conversions of existing sites. Sets deadlines, assigns responsibilities, and personally tracks and unblocks progress. Prepares reports for upper management regarding the status of all projects.
Requires a bachelor's degree and at least 4 years of project management experience in power infrastructure, electrical systems, hydrogen/fuel cell systems, or a related area. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, detail-oriented operator who thrives in ambiguity, dives deep into technical and schedule details, and acts with urgency rather than waiting for direction. Must be familiar with a variety of the field's concepts, practices, and procedures across both power and hydrogen domains. Relies on sound judgment to plan and accomplish goals, and is comfortable rolling up sleeves — walking the site, reading the drawings, chasing the long-lead order, and closing out the punch list. Leads and directs the work of contractors, vendors, and cross-functional teams. A wide degree of creativity and latitude is expected to solve complex energy infrastructure challenges across diverse site conditions and regulatory environments. Typically reports to a manager or head of a unit/department.
Key job responsibilities
Project Management & Bias for Action
• Own delivery end to end and act with urgency — move projects forward every day rather than waiting for direction or escalation
• Get into the details: read the drawings, interrogate the schedule, understand the single-line and the hydrogen P&ID, and verify the numbers personally
• Be hands-on and in the field — walk the site, attend installation and commissioning activities, and verify work directly rather than relying solely on status reports
• Build and maintain the plan of record: detailed schedules, critical-path analysis, dependencies, risks, and clear owners and dates
• Proactively identify blockers and drive them to closure; dive deep on root cause and remove obstacles for contractors and cross-functional teams
• Run a tight operating rhythm — stand-ups, weekly reviews, and crisp written updates that make status and risks unambiguous
• Make decisions with incomplete information, bias toward action, and course-correct quickly as new data emerges
Program Coordination & Oversight
• Responsible for the coordination and completion of multiple simultaneous power and hydrogen execution projects across U.S. sites
• Oversee all aspects of the execution program from feasibility through commissioning and handover
• Set deadlines, assign responsibilities, and monitor and summarize the progress of all projects
• Prepare reports for upper management regarding program status, including monthly flash updates and executive summaries
• Lead and direct the work of contractors, vendors, consultants, and cross-functional teams
• Perform a variety of tasks ranging from technical design review to stakeholder management to regulatory coordination
Amazon Standards, Specifications & Quality Assurance
• Follow and verify that Amazon standards, specifications, and processes are met across all power and hydrogen infrastructure installations
• Ensure electrical equipment, switchgear, generators, fuel cells, hydrogen storage/dispensing systems, and associated systems comply with Amazon technical standards and design requirements
• Conduct quality reviews at each project phase to validate adherence to Amazon specifications before progressing to the next milestone
• Verify vendor deliverables, shop drawings, and equipment submittals meet Amazon engineering standards
• Coordinate with Amazon internal engineering teams to resolve specification questions and obtain approvals
• Document and track any deviations from Amazon specifications, securing proper waivers or corrective actions (e.g., Supplier Corrective Action Reports / SCARs)
Power Capacity Execution
• Drive execution of temporary and permanent power deployment projects — utility upgrades, generator installations, switchgear deployments, and service upgrades
• Oversee deployment of temporary and permanent natural gas and diesel generator systems (1–5MW scale), including rental genset mobilization and conversion to permanent power
• Manage utility coordination including transformer upgrades, switchgear installations, and service upgrades with utility companies
• Own the end-to-end switchgear (SWGR) procurement process: specification development, vendor selection, purchase order issuance, and delivery tracking
• Track SWGR lead times (typically 10–26 weeks) across all sites and ensure orders are placed to meet project timelines; monitor factory acceptance testing (FAT) and coordinate site delivery logistics
• Review and validate electrical designs, single-line diagrams, load calculations, and power distribution configurations
• Ensure compliance with NEC, NFPA, and local electrical codes
Hydrogen Fuel Cell Execution
• Decommissioning: Plan and execute safe decommissioning of existing hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cell assets — isolation, purging/inerting, asset removal, site restoration, and disposition in accordance with Amazon standards and applicable safety codes
• Infrastructure & fuel cell launch: Lead the launch of new hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cells per Amazon standards and processes — hydrogen storage and dispensing systems, hydrogen pads, piping, fueling infrastructure, and fuel cell power modules, from design review through installation, commissioning, and startup
• Conversions: Manage conversions of existing sites to hydrogen fuel cell operation (or between configurations), coordinating the transition sequencing, infrastructure modifications, and cutover to minimize operational disruption
• Coordinate with hydrogen fuel cell vendors and OEMs (e.g., Plug Power and equivalents) on equipment specifications, delivery schedules, and field support
• Verify hydrogen systems meet Amazon specifications and applicable hydrogen safety and fire codes (e.g., NFPA 2, NFPA 55) throughout design, installation, and commissioning
• Oversee fuel cell capacity planning, dispenser configuration, and integration with site power and operations
Procurement & Long-Lead Equipment Management
• Own procurement for long-lead equipment across both domains — switchgear, generators, fuel cells, and hydrogen infrastructure components
• Specify, order, track lead times, verify specifications, and coordinate delivery for critical-path equipment
• Coordinate with manufacturers and vendors on custom configurations and delivery schedules
• Escalate equipment delivery risks immediately when lead times threaten project schedules
Permitting & Regulatory
• Own the permitting process for all sites — air permit applications for stationary generator installations and hydrogen-related permits and approvals
• Prepare and submit permit applications across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory environments; track application status, agency review timelines, and approval milestones for each site
• Navigate complex permitting scenarios including CEQA approvals, non-attainment areas, emission offset requirements, and hydrogen/fire code approvals
• Coordinate with environmental and fire/life-safety consultants to develop applications, emission calculations, and hazard analyses
• Maintain a permit tracking log with submission dates, agency contacts, expected approval dates, and required follow-ups
• Proactively identify permitting risks and develop contingency plans to avoid schedule impacts; ensure all required emission and safety data is obtained from generator and fuel cell vendors
Project Execution & Delivery
• Drive the end-to-end project lifecycle: feasibility, design, procurement, permitting, installation, commissioning, and handover
• Develop and maintain detailed project schedules, budgets, risk registers, and status reports
• Coordinate contractor mobilization, equipment procurement, and installation activities
• Identify and resolve critical-path blockers with urgency; escalate issues proactively
• Rely on extensive experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals under compressed timelines
Stakeholder Management
• Serve as the primary point of contact and single-threaded owner across all project stakeholders, aligning internal and external parties and holding each accountable to deliverables and timelines
• Customer — Amazon Operations: partner with Amazon Operations (the internal customer) to understand site requirements, manage expectations, minimize operational disruption, and secure buy-in through launch and handover
• General Contractor (GC): direct and hold the GC accountable for construction scope, schedule, RFIs, submittals, and field execution
• Engineer of Record (EOR) & Architect of Record (AOR): coordinate design intent, drawing reviews, RFIs, and design changes; ensure the installed work conforms to the stamped design
• Electrical Contractor (EC): coordinate electrical installation, terminations, testing, and energization activities and sequencing
• Air permitting agencies & consultants: engage regulatory agencies and environmental consultants (e.g., Trinity) to secure and maintain air permits and keep applications on the critical path
• Utility engagement — gas pipeline: drive utility coordination for natural gas pipeline connections, metering, pressure requirements, service applications, and interconnection timelines
• Equipment vendors & OEMs: manage generator, switchgear, fuel cell, and hydrogen infrastructure vendors on specifications, lead times, and field support
• Coordinate with Property/Construction Managers (PCMs) and Construction Managers at each site
• Provide weekly status updates and monthly program reports to leadership
Site Launches, Commissioning & Energization
• Travel to project sites during critical installation, commissioning, and decommissioning phases
• Oversee equipment startup, testing, and acceptance procedures for both power and hydrogen systems
• Ensure safe energization, hydrogen system startup, and transition to operations

- 4+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams

description:
Our systems are at the core of Amazon.com. We serve the product and offering catalog containing billions of records, and we are the authority for product information, including availability and price. Our systems respond to billions of requests per day that power the Amazon shopping experiences and other customer interfaces, such as Amazon Shopping App, Kindle, Wholefoods, Amazon Fresh and Amazon Alexa. We are regularly challenged by new business use-cases that bring in high levels of ambiguity and competing priorities. Our team has been instrumental in launching high-impact customer features, such as "Buy For Me" that helps customers discover and seamlessly purchase select products from other brands’ sites if those items are not currently sold in Amazon’s store. By building segmented offers, we helped Amazon provide sub-same-day delivery to our customers and achieve the fastest delivery speeds in the US last year. These systems source data from many data sources and execute logic to determine buyability of the items in the Amazon catalog, which is consumed by hundreds of systems.

title: AI Applied Scientist, AI Evaluation Science
description:
AI systems are only as trustworthy as the methods used to evaluate them. At Apple, where AI powers experiences for billions of people, getting evaluation right is not a support function, it is a foundational science. Our team, part of Apple Services Engineering, is building that scientific foundation: rigorous, scalable evaluation methodology for LLMs, agentic systems, and human-AI interaction. Our goal is evidence that teams can act on: what to measure, whether a change helped, why a system failed, and whether it is ready to ship.
What makes this team unusual is its interdisciplinary core. You will work alongside measurement scientists (psychometrics, validity theory), ML researchers, and platform engineers, bringing together ML research, statistical rigor, and production engineering.
We are looking for an Applied Scientist who works across the full arc of evaluation science: turning research into tools engineers can use on their own, and turning what those engineers run into new research. You care whether a method holds up on real data, at real scale, for a real decision, and you are curious enough to go after the open question underneath when it doesn't.
Our team is building self-service evaluation: tools, SDKs, and AI-powered capabilities that let engineers across Apple evaluate their AI features on their own, quickly and correctly, so they can build and ship those features faster. You will develop the methods that make this possible: raising the quality of the evaluations engineers run, and helping them understand what their results mean and what to do next. Often the method a problem needs doesn't exist yet. When that happens, you will figure it out, whether that means extending a recent paper or developing something new, and share what you learn through publications and internal research reports. We are looking for individuals across a range of experience levels.
With research and measurement scientists, you will co-develop new methods, make sure the tools give engineers valid, trustworthy signals, and bring back the hard problems that should shape the team's research agenda. With platform and research engineers, you will define what each method needs to work reliably without an expert in the loop, including its assumptions, failure modes, and validation tests, so it can ship in the evaluation SDKs and APIs used across Apple.
The successful candidate combines scientific depth with practical judgment: you know which methods fit a problem and why, can design experiments that show whether they actually work, can diagnose why they break down on messy real-world data, and can explain clearly what an evaluation result does and does not support.
Minimum qualifications: Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, or a closely related field, or a Master's degree in one of these fields with 3+ years of applied research experience.
Deep expertise in evaluating AI systems, gained through research on evaluation methods, substantial hands-on experience evaluating LLMs or agentic systems in real products, or both.
Strong proficiency in Python and the modern ML ecosystem, with demonstrated ability to implement complex methods from recent papers and run large-scale experiments.
Hands-on experience with large language models, whether fine-tuning, inference, prompting pipelines, or building LLM-powered applications.
Demonstrated research ability through publications at peer-reviewed venues, preprints, or equivalent research output.
Track record of applying research to practical problems: methods, prototypes, or tools adopted by other teams or used to inform real product decisions.
Solid software engineering fundamentals for research code: version control, testing, reproducibility, and code others can build on.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex results, and their limitations, to diverse audiences.
Comfort with ambiguity and new problem spaces; you thrive when building something that doesn't yet have a playbook.
Preferred qualifications: First-author publications at top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP), especially on evaluation methodology: papers about how to evaluate, not just papers that use evaluation to demonstrate model improvements.
Specific experience in one or more of: LLM-as-judge approaches (calibration, rubric design, bias mitigation); benchmark design and validation (IRT, contamination detection); human evaluation methodology (protocol design, quality control); experimentation and comparisons between system versions (A/B testing, uncertainty quantification); or agentic and multi-agent system evaluation, including failure diagnosis and automated red-teaming.
Familiarity with theoretical foundations of evaluation: measurement theory and validity frameworks, statistical learning theory (calibration, reliability, decision theory), causal inference, or preference aggregation.
Experience with the practical challenges of evaluating generative AI and agentic systems: non-deterministic outputs, token economics, multi-turn agent trajectories, and tool use.
Experience building methods or tools used directly by non-experts, such as developer-facing ML tooling or self-service analytics.
Familiarity with modern evaluation tools and frameworks (e.g., DeepEval, Ragas, TruLens, LangSmith, or agent tracing and observability tools).
Experience working with distributed computing or cloud-native tooling (e.g., Ray, Spark, Docker/Kubernetes) to run evaluations at scale.
Experience with cross-disciplinary work, such as collaboration with social scientists, psychometricians, or domain experts.
Experience in fast-moving, early-stage teams where you helped define technical direction from the ground up.

title: AI Measurement Scientist, AI Evaluation Platform
description:
Apple is where individual imaginations gather together, committing to the values that lead to great work. Every new product we build, service we create, or experience we deliver is the result of us making each other's ideas stronger.
Our team, part of Apple Services Engineering, is building the scientific foundation for how AI systems are evaluated across Apple. Our goal is to create the evidence that teams can act on: what to measure, whether a change helped, why a system failed, and whether it is ready to ship. We are seeking a Measurement Scientist to ensure that our evaluation methods are not just sophisticated, but scientifically valid and trustworthy. In this role, you will apply apply state-of-the-art measurement methods, validity frameworks, experimental design, and statistical rigor to establish measurement standards for AI evaluation, ensuring that when we claim an evaluator measures "helpfulness" or "safety," it actually does. We are looking for individuals across a range of experience levels.
This role uniquely bridges measurement science and cutting-edge AI evaluation. This role uniquely bridges measurement science and cutting-edge AI evaluation. Our team is building AI tools and capabilities to help developers do evaluation better and faster. You will develop methods for validating these tools: making sure that they generate evaluation artifacts and workflows that give developers the right signals to make sound engineering decisions and build great products for Apple customers.
You will work on an interdisciplinary team with with other measurement scientists and ML researchers to solve new problems in AI evaluation. Your work will be both published at top measurement and ML venues and productionized into the evaluation SDK used across Apple. The successful candidate will have deep expertise in psychometrics or other measurement disciplines, or in experimental design and causal inference, with the ability to apply these principles to novel AI evaluation challenges. Our team deliberately combines ML science and measurement science. We especially welcome people who bridge those areas, including computer scientists who specialize in measurement, and measurement scientists who have worked on ML problems. You will also work collaboratively with platform engineers and evaluation practitioners to translate measurement science into practical tools that scale across the organization.
Minimum qualifications: PhD in Computer Science or Machine Learning with a measurement or evaluation focus, Psychometrics, Educational Measurement, Quantitative Psychology, Statistics, Biostatistics, Econometrics, or equivalent research/work experience.
Deep expertise in modeling test or benchmark data (IRT, latent variable, or other response models) and construct validation, in benchmark design and validity for AI systems, or in experimental design and causal inference (surrogate outcomes, observational causal methods).
Strong statistical foundation including experimental design, power analysis, sampling theory, and uncertainty quantification.
Track record of designing and validating measurement instruments or experiments as demonstrated through publications or applied work.
Proficiency in Python (preferred) or R for statistical analysis, psychometric modeling, and method implementation.
Strong working knowledge of generative AI technology.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain complex measurement concepts to engineers, ML researchers, and non-technical stakeholders.
Preferred qualifications: Research or experience applying measurement science to AI/ML evaluation, benchmark validity, automated scoring systems, or computational assessment.
Knowledge of modern ML evaluation challenges including LLM-as-judge, automated metrics, benchmark design, and agentic systems.
Publications at measurement venues or top ML conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR).
Expertise in computational social or behavioral science using generative AI.
Experience collaborating with engineers to turn research methods into production tools and scalable infrastructure.
Experience with online experimentation or with validating offline metrics against real-world outcomes (surrogate or proxy metrics).
Experience estimating rare events or making decisions when one kind of error costs far more than another.

title: AIML - Senior Machine Learning Platform Engineer, Responsible AI and Safety
description:
Join us in shaping the future of Generative AI at Apple! Are you passionate about making AI systems safer, more inclusive, and globally representative? Apple is seeking a Machine Learning Platform Engineer to build the tooling and infrastructure behind our Responsible AI mitigations, from on-device foundation models running on Apple Silicon to server-side inference on Private Cloud Compute (PCC). In this role, you will build the Python platform our ML and safety engineers rely on to train, evaluate, deploy, and configure safety classifiers, guardrail models, and model behavior overrides. You will turn manual, one-off workflows into automated, scalable, and reproducible systems, so that every evaluation runs the same way, every deployment is validated, and every configuration change is safe to ship
Our team leads Responsible AI initiatives for global generative AI products, operating at the intersection of policy, product, and GenAI. We build the safety guardrails, and policy enforcement layers that protect users from unintended model behavior. This role builds the platform underneath that work. You will build the systems that enable consistent training and evaluation at scale: an training/evaluation platform that runs any benchmark the same way every time, deployment pipelines that package and release models and mitigation assets to devices and the cloud, and tooling that lets engineers across many languages and modalities author and validate configuration changes with confidence. You will also dig into the failures and regressions the platform surfaces, and turn them into concrete fixes. ML engineers, client engineers, policy, and release teams are your customers, and you will need enough understanding of how models are evaluated and served to build infrastructure whose results they can trust.

BS in Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience
Experience building infrastructure or tooling for ML inference, evaluation, or deployment that is used by engineers outside your direct team
Experience building or operating infrastructure that deploys ML models to production and maintains them across versions
Working knowledge of how ML models are evaluated (metrics, held-out test sets, error analysis, sources of non-reproducibility), enough to build evaluation infrastructure whose results ML engineers can trust
Experience designing configuration-driven systems, including schemas, validation, versioning, and safe rollout of config changes
Strong software engineering fundamentals: testing, CI/CD, code review, and writing maintainable code that others build on
Excellent communication skills and the ability to explain technical tradeoffs to cross-functional partners

Working knowledge of on-device ML runtimes (Core ML, MLX, or equivalent) and the model-export lifecycle: converting trained models into shippable assets and loading them at runtime
Experience running distributed evaluation or workflow orchestration at scale (Kubernetes, Ray, Spark, or equivalent)

Experience building LLM-based or agentic developer tooling
Familiarity with Swift

title: AMR Regional Crisis Manager
description:
Do you instinctively know when to take action? Do you excel in high-pressure situations? Then a career at Apple might be for you. As part of Apple’s Global Security team, you’ll safeguard our most valuable assets—our people and innovations. Working alongside a dedicated team, you’ll develop and implement crisis management strategies to protect Apple’s operations, employees, and assets across its facilities and global supply chain, ensuring resilience against emerging threats and disruptions.

Success in this role requires expertise in crisis management, tactical problem-solving, and strong stakeholder engagement.

• Develop a comprehensive understanding of Apple’s assets across business units.

• Quickly identify and assess risks to Apple during incidents.

Global perspective in addressing crisis challenges
Experience developing and implementing proactive crisis response plans

Ability to distill complex information into clear, concise communication

Strong track record of delivering on commitments and acknowledging mistakes when necessary
Exceptional attention to detail and standards
Ability to assess and test local response capabilities and CRT readiness

title: AR/VR Software Engineer, Spatial Experiences - Vision Products Software
description:
We are a small, close-knit team of engineers building the experiences that let people view, place, and share 3D content across Apple platforms, including Apple Vision Pro. title: Administrative Assistant, Intelligent System Experience
description:

title: Battery Algorithm and Model Calibration Engineer

title: Bluetooth/Thread Embedded Software Engineer, Wireless Technologies & Ecosystems
description:

title: Cellular RF Systems Architect - RF Configuration
description:
At Apple, our work is dedicated to creating products that connect and enrich people's lives. The Cellular RF Systems Engineering team sits at the very core of that mission, defining the wireless technologies that enable seamless experiences for hundreds of millions of users worldwide.
We are looking for a cellular RF engineer to translate complex 5G and 6G use cases into optimized RF configurations that bring our products to life. Configurations define how the transceiver and front-end are set up for each band, band combination, and use case, including signal routing, port mapping, gain and linearity modes and front-end control settings. If you enjoy structuring complex systems, building tools that make work scale, and connecting RF hardware and software teams, this role is for you.
In this role, you will be responsible for the optimal interaction between our RF transceivers and RF front-end modules. You will turn advanced cellular capabilities, such as carrier aggregation, MIMO, SRS antenna switching and Multi-SIM into concrete transceiver and front-end configurations. You will work closely with transmitter and receiver teams to define and refine these configurations, and partner with hardware, software and validation teams to bring them into our products. You will develop tooling and automation that keep configurations consistent across programs and contribute to the system design documentation that guides implementation.

Experience applying AI/ML to solve system-level optimization problems.
History of successfully balancing cutting-edge hardware innovation with the practical constraints of high-volume manufacturing.

description:

Join Apple, and help us leave the world better than we found it.
The Commercial and Strategy Management (CSM) team is part of the Manufacturing Design Organization responsible for commercial strategy, negotiations, and cost management for mechanical enclosure components across Apple’s products. The CSM team works with our partners in Operations as well as Engineering do develop the best cost strategy and deals to support Apple’s product roadmap.
Commercial and Strategy Managers sit at the intersection of Apple's business activities and engineering communities and balance the needs of both groups to ensure successful product launches with competitive costs.

Ability to toggle between strategic and detail oriented thinking
Tenacious problem solving & issue resolution skills
Excellent presentation and interpersonal skills
Ability to influence across multiple functional teams

Excellent communicators, capable of working in multinational environments, driven and motivated by accomplishing extraordinary objectives
Mechanical and/or prior technical acumen to effectively negotiate by leveraging manufacturing process and product design fundamentals

title: Custom Circuit RTL Design Engineer
description:
Do you love creating elegant solutions to highly complex challenges? Do you intrinsically see the importance in every detail? As part of our Silicon Technologies group, you’ll help design and manufacture our next-generation, high-performance, power-efficient processor, system-on-chip (SoC). You’ll ensure Apple products and services can seamlessly and efficiently handle the tasks that make them beloved by millions. Joining this group means you’ll be responsible for crafting and building the technology that fuels Apple’s devices. Together, you and your team will enable our customers to do all the things they love with their devices. Do you have a passion for crafting entirely new solutions?
As part of our Digital Circuits Group, youʼll take imaginative and revolutionary ideas and determine how to turn them into reality! You and your team will apply engineering fundamentals and start from scratch if needed, bringing forward-thinking ideas to the real world! Your efforts will be groundbreaking, often literally. Join us, and youʼll help design the tools that allow us to bring customers experiences they have never-before envisioned. You will be part of an exciting silicon design group that is responsible for designing pioneering ASICs. In this role as a Custom Circuit RTL Design Engineer, you will be working with the custom circuits team to implement behavioral and structural RTL models of advanced custom digital circuits, translate specifications in assertions models, and verify equivalence of the RTL models to circuits. You will be at the heart of a processor design effort, making a critical impact delivering products to market quickly.
In this highly visible role as a Custom Circuits RTL Design Engineer, you will be at the center of a SoC design effort collaborating with all teams, with a critical impact on getting bug-free functional products to market quickly. This requires you to work closely with the circuit design team to review design and architecture specifications and with various design teams across the SoC partitions to understand the use cases and corner conditions to develop test plans. Furthermore, you will be required to develop the methodology for test benches and coverage monitors for functional coverage and assertions. You will also work on improving the RTL methodology as applicable to simulation and emulation scenarios.
You will have the responsibilities as follows:
- Design and implement behavioral RTL models for various custom SRAM arrays.
- Work with logic/architecture team to determine specifications and assertions for custom SRAM arrays.
- Work closely with custom circuit team to review schematics and understand how the RTL must model it.
- Work closely with DV teams to verify functionality.
- Work with SOC teams to successfully integrate custom RTL design into chip.
- Implement RTL methodology and new flows with understanding of GenAI capabilities and limitations in hardware design to successfully integrate custom RTL design into chip.
- Use GenAI assisted tools for faster debug and turnaround time.
Minimum qualifications: BS and a minimum of 3 years of relevant industry experience
Preferred qualifications: In-depth knowledge of digital design, behavioral (including emulation-friendly) and structural RTL coding especially as it pertains to SRAM and register file design
Knowledge of Verilog, System Verilog and experience with industry standard simulators and waveform debugging tools
Knowledge of regression and revision control tools, and scripting language (python / perl)
Knowledge of industry standard design and verification tools, such as ESPCV and/or LEC
Knowledge of regression and revision control tools.
Basic knowledge of viewing and understanding custom circuit schematics
Knowledge of custom circuit and SRAM design and DFT (ATPG/MBIST) is desirable.

title: Design Ops - Integrated Producer
description:
Apple TV's Marketing team crafts world-class campaigns that connect audiences with high-quality stories — building brand awareness and loyalty. We drive innovation and excellence — from strategic vision to creative execution — collaborating across the Apple ecosystem, as well as agencies, studios, and talent to place Apple TV at the heart of global culture.
The Operations team within Apple TV Marketing is tasked with building processes/workflows, managing budgets, and facilitating all creative production in partnership with our creative teams. Within Operations, the Integrated Producer works in lockstep with our Creative Directors, Art Directors and Strategists, as well as a multitude of cross-functional partners and external agencies, ensuring all key art, OOH, digital, and social assets are produced and delivered across a variety of multi-channel paid, owned, and earned channels -- all in support of Apple TV original series, films, brand, and most recently, sports. While the Creative and Strategy leads are establishing the “what” and the “why” of our campaign assets & strategy, the Operations team — more specifically, the Producers — are driving the “how.”
* Produce & project manage all artwork, HID, motion, and social assets – from initial kick off through approvals and final delivery.
* Elevate the creative work by defining and driving all workflow, execution, and production processes/strategies.
* Lead multiple projects in parallel, prioritizing and communicating action items across competing deadlines and campaigns.
* Serve as the source of truth & central hub for all creative status information, updating tools, decks, and documents with dates, schedules, and next steps — ensuring all internal parties are informed as the overall status evolves by the day (or even minute).

* Liase with external agencies to communicate action items and due dates, providing a sense of prioritization in the face of expanding/evolving cross-functional needs
* Ensure agencies have access to any source assets, including video, art, & photography, to build best-in-class creative
* Seeing around corners to recognize potential challenges and pivoting accordingly.
* Brainstorm new ways of working to continually scale our production workflows

Bachelor’s Degree in Marketing, Communications, or related field
Experience in marketing or entertainment
History with internal and third party software tools that focus on asset/project management, as well as creative-based tools, like the Adobe suite, etc.

The ability to positively collaborate in a creative environment across a wide variety of internal/external teams, individuals, and personalities

description:

As an EMC Design Manager in Austin, you will lead a small, highly capable team of EMC design engineers. title: Principal Security Architect, Data Center Security
description:
The Apple Services Engineering Security team is looking for a principal-level security architect to own end-to-end trust for Apple’s next generation of data center infrastructure, the assurance that every physical and logical component, from silicon to the running workload, operates in a known, verifiable, tamper-evident state, and that this trust can be cryptographically proven to any relying party before access or data is granted. This spans hardware root of trust, DPU/IPU offload security, software and workload integrity, and the attestation protocols that tie them together into a single verifiable chain. You will partner with silicon, firmware, SOC architecture, platform, and cloud infrastructure teams to design and integrate this stack, and you’ll represent Apple in the standards bodies that define how this trust travels across the industry.
You will architect and integrate security across four layers of the data center stack:
Hardware root of trust — secure boot chains anchored in silicon (fuses, eFuse-based identity, HSMs), platform firmware integrity (UEFI/BIOS measured boot), and the physical/supply-chain controls that establish an immutable, device-unique identity at power-on.
IPU/DPU and offload security — working with platform and networking teams to ensure SmartNICs/DPUs/IPUs, as the emerging trust boundary isolating tenant workloads from infrastructure management, have their own attestable root of trust, not just line-rate crypto and policy enforcement.
Software and workload integrity — measured, signed boot through hypervisor/OS/container runtime with an unbroken chain of custody from firmware to running workload; confidential computing primitives (enclaves, TEEs, confidential VMs); drift detection against measured baselines.
Attestation and verifiable trust — the mechanism that converts the above into a dynamic, per-session trust decision: signed quotes of measured state, verification against golden measurements, key sealing/unsealing tied to attestation results, revocation of compromised measurements, and remote attestation protocols that let this trust travel to the relying party that needs it, including the agent identity layer sitting on top of this stack.
You will drive design reviews and threat models with SOC architects and platform teams, define the architecture that lets each layer attest up to the next, and ensure quality and agility through rigorous testing, participating in on-call for the systems you ship.
Minimum qualifications: 10+ years of security/software engineering experience, including systems-level and infrastructure security
Deep, hands-on experience with hardware root-of-trust architectures (TPM, DICE, or equivalent) and measured/attested boot chains
Proven track record designing or implementing remote attestation protocols, key sealing/provisioning tied to attestation state, and measurement revocation

The future is being defined right now, and the Swift Standard Libraries team is at the center of it. The work we do will shape the developer experience on Apple's platforms and beyond for decades to come.
The Swift Standard Libraries team is responsible for much of the user-facing experience of the Swift programming language via the Standard Library and Foundation, which reaches from basic types and data structures like Date and String to complex algorithms like sorting and calendrical calculation. The team also develops a growing roster of open-source Swift packages including Algorithms, Argument Parser, Async Algorithms, Atomics, Numerics, Collections, System and Subprocess. You will join a small team of thoughtful, versatile engineers in meeting the challenge of designing correct and expressive high-level APIs with carefully tuned low-level implementations. You'll work mostly in the open as an active contributor to the swift.org open-source project, collaborating with the Swift compiler team, engineers from across every part of Apple, and the Swift open-source community.
Our team strives to build a diverse, inclusive team and healthy, balanced work environment. We believe that every engineer brings unique skills and perspective. Far more than any specific experience or skill, we are looking for engineers who want to enable others to build great software, while learning and developing their skills.

Interest in programming language and library design, and engage with the open-source community
The ability to simplify complex ideas and explain them clearly
Preferred qualifications: Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science or equivalent experience.

title: US Consumer Retail & PC Insights Lead
description:
The people here at Apple donʼt just build products— they craft the kind of wonder thatʼs revolutionized entire industries. Itʼs the diversity of those people and their ideas that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do, from amazing technology to industry-leading environmental efforts. Join Apple, and help us leave the world better than we found it.
Appleʼs US Sales organization generates the revenue needed to fuel our ongoing development of products and services. This in turn, enriches the lives of hundreds of millions of people around the world. We are, in many ways, the face of Apple to our largest customers.
Within US Sales, the Business Planning & Strategic Insights team acts as the strategic market radar across our national retailer computing portfolio, educating sales and product leaders on competitive threats, consumer behavior shifts, and category growth opportunities. We are seeking a US Consumer Retail & PC Insights Lead to serve as our primary market and category expert. In this role, you will partner directly with Consumer Sales leadership, Finance, Business Operations and Business Development functions to analyze computing industry and channel dynamics, evaluate competitor pricing and new product introduction (NPI) moves, and provide recommendations on how to defend and grow Apple’s market positioning within the category.
In this role, you will:
- Own weekly, monthly, quarterly and annual market lens of forecasting and planning, articulating market dynamics (units, competitive pricing and campaigns, reseller insights and portfolio evolution as well as customer insights).
- Build the market center of excellence for computing (notebooks, desktops, tablets) to articulate implications of market dynamics on future sales in partnership with Finance and Sales leadership. Conduct competitive teardowns of competitor NPIs and go-to-market campaigns and track promotional elasticity and competitor deal badging across tentpole moments (Back-to-School, Prime Day, Black Friday/Holiday).
- Develop and assess insightful customer trends and market shifts about the dynamic US Consumer landscape, making key recommendations that utilize market share and improve profit opportunities feeding into Business Development, Operations, and WW Product Marketing.
- Own syndicated data intelligence and work with 3P market intelligence vendors to distill market trends. Ensure the resources for regular reporting requirements of the business are in place, dependable and high quality. Support automating and leverage automated intelligence platforms to translate market movements into executive category insights for Sales leadership.
- Coordinate and drive cross-functional category reviews to assess the state of the computing business, share market share opportunities, and seek feedback from leadership on strategic direction.
- Monitor market trends and competitive dynamics across retail price bands that create new opportunities and risks for Apple's computing portfolio.
- Through a continuous improvement attitude, identify new analytical methodologies and visualization techniques to turn data into insights and action.
- Communicate effectively within the team and to other colleagues; providing consistent support to Sales leadership.
- Represent decisions and recommendations from analysis to relevant parties within the global virtual research and analytics function.
Minimum qualifications: 8+ years experience in meaningful positions encompassing consumer/business intelligence, consumer product marketing, product management, commercial management, market research, and/or strategic planning
Proven knowledge of relevant market drivers across the value chain
Experience with multifaceted analytical methodologies and their application through best practices in commercial and consumer environments.
Experience in category management and decision-making process of external customers
Excellent numeracy and data management skills
Deep understanding of consumer trends and their potential impact on the business
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required
Preferred qualifications: Commercial insight experience in complex consumer electronic retailer and commercial markets, ideally with deep familiarity with the computing domain (notebooks, desktops, tablets)
Experience within the US consumer and commercial routes to market preferred
Exceptional decision-making ability to transform complex market data into actionable insights, category plans, and commercial vision
MBA preferred

Excellent organization skills.
Excellent communication skills – both written and oral.

• Low-latency design for time-critical test traffic
• Secure onboarding of thousands of device

Python and Bash development skills: building and maintaining tools others rely on, with

Industry certifications such as CWNE, CWNA, CWDP, CWAP, or vendor equivalents

title: NPI Technician
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a New Product Introduction (NPI) Technician at Base, you’ll play a hands-on role in bringing new battery products and manufacturing processes from early prototypes to full production. You’ll support prototype builds, validate manufacturing processes, and ensure each trial meets product specifications. Along the way, you’ll document observations, collaborate with cross-functional teams, and help refine processes that will eventually scale across our production lines. This role offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of engineering and manufacturing while helping turn new ideas into real, scalable products.

 

What You’ll Do

 - Support prototype builds and trial runs for new products and manufacturing processes

 - Assist in validating manufacturing processes to ensure product specifications are consistently achieved

 - Test and validate systems and components to support quality assurance procedures

 - Document observations during build trials and capture the state of assembly and process performance

 - Read and follow manufacturing instructions, mechanical drawings, and basic electrical documentation

 - Collaborate with engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams to evaluate and refine production processes

 - Provide feedback during change control and process improvement discussions

 

What You’ll Bring

 - Experience supporting prototype builds, pre-production runs, or early manufacturing trials

 - Basic understanding of electrical and mechanical systems

 - Ability to read and interpret manufacturing instructions and mechanical drawings, with basic electrical knowledge

 - High level of craftsmanship and attention to detail while maintaining speed and efficiency

 - Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities

 - Comfortable working across multiple projects and collaborating with cross-functional teams

 - Reliable, proactive, and quality-focused with strong initiative

 

About the Team

The New Product Introduction (NPI) team is responsible for bridging the gap between engineering design and scalable manufacturing at Base. Every prototype build, process validation, and trial run helps transform early concepts into reliable production systems. Your work will directly shape how our batteries are built at scale, refining the processes that power the factories of the future. As part of this team, you’ll collaborate closely with engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams while gaining exposure to cutting-edge battery technology and advanced production systems.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. We are working on building autonomous delivery robots from the ground-up and other automation solutions as part of DoorDash's core delivery platform. Ability to evaluate complex trade-offs, identify failure modes, and translate ambiguous business and regulatory goals into precise, verifiable engineering specifications

About the Team
Audience Insights brings the voices of consumers, Dashers and merchants into decisions across DoorDash. Our work spans audiences, markets and business problems, giving researchers the opportunity to apply their skills in many different ways. We are expanding how we connect learning globally, combine survey and behavioral data, and use AI to find patterns in quantitative and qualitative research.
About the Role
In this remote US role, you will lead brand insights, helping the business set the right goals, track progress and improve creative before and after launch. You will lead 3 manager-level roles, including 1 opening, with Canada in the direct team and dotted-line consultation for Australia and other markets and brands. You will own work end to end while developing the team and shaping the next chapter of our brand-to-business learning. You will report into the Head of Audience Insights on our Audience Insights team in our Marketing organization.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Shape brand goals: Guide meaningful metrics and targets grounded in history, business context and the decisions partners need to make.
Own the brand foundation: Lead tracking across audiences and measurement levels, protect quality and comparability, and turn reporting and ad hoc analyses into actionable insight.
Improve creative: Lead pre- and post-testing and build focused diagnostics that guide campaign development and specific optimizations.
Connect the evidence: Combine survey, behavioral and qualitative learning, use AI thoughtfully, and identify new opportunities and future analytical questions in existing data.
Develop people and drive decisions: Coach managers, guide vendors and partners across markets, and deliver reports and presentations that shape marketing strategy and action.
We’re excited about you because…
You bring deep research experience: You have 8+ years in Market Research or Insights, with end-to-end ownership of studies that inform brand and marketing decisions.
