title: Product Manager - Chicago, IL
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
Impact In This Role:
As a Product Manager at MISUMI Americas, you will own a defined product area — whether a feature set, a workflow, a capability, or a segment of our platform — and be responsible for delivering strong, well-executed product work within it. You will gather and synthesize customer, stakeholder, and performance insights; write clear requirements; partner closely with Engineering and Design on delivery; and track outcomes to drive continuous improvement.
This role is designed for someone who is serious about the craft of product management and is ready to build the depth of judgment and business understanding needed to take on broader ownership over time. You will be expected to deliver reliably, communicate clearly, build credibility with your cross-functional partners, and show increasing independence as you develop fluency in the domain. The best PMs in this role will grow into Senior PMs who own full product areas with strategic autonomy.
You will report to the VP, Product Management.
Areas of Responsibility:
Business acumen and domain awareness
Develop a deep understanding of the customers, internal users, and business context relevant to your product area — including how your work connects to broader platform goals and company priorities
Research and synthesize customer needs, stakeholder feedback, and operational realities to build a clear, grounded point of view on the problems your team should be solving
Assess the needs of internal users across Operations, Sales, and other functions, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and remove friction in workflows that touch your area
Stay current on how your product area is performing — tracking metrics, monitoring trends, and developing hypotheses about where the biggest opportunities for improvement lie
Build familiarity with the competitive landscape and with how MISUMI Americas' platform capabilities compare to alternatives available to our customers
Roadmap contribution, work analysis, and scoping
Contribute to roadmap development within your area with increasing independence, translating high-level goals into clearly scoped objectives, projects, and requirements
Develop and maintain a framework for tracking input and output metrics that provide a quantitative view of the success and impact of your work
Build business cases for prioritized initiatives, articulating the customer value, business rationale, and expected outcomes in a way that earns stakeholder confidence
Scope and define requirements for roadmap items with clarity and specificity — ensuring Engineering and Design have what they need to build the right thing, efficiently
Proactively identify trade-offs and risks associated with scope and sequencing decisions, and work collaboratively with your team to develop pragmatic mitigation approaches
Establish and communicate a well-reasoned point of view on the problems your team should prioritize and why
Cross-functional collaboration
Build strong working relationships with Engineering, Design, Operations, Sales, and other functions — earning trust through clear communication, good judgment, and consistent follow-through
Lead cross-functional meetings within your area to align on scope, priorities, and requirements — ensuring that all relevant perspectives are heard and decisions are made with shared understanding
Actively seek feedback from stakeholders and adjust plans accordingly, fostering a responsive and collaborative approach to product development
Work with cross-functional partners to develop and evaluate hypotheses about customer needs and solutions, bringing both rigor and creativity to discovery
Communicate team progress and results to stakeholders with transparency — celebrating wins and ensuring the organization learns from setbacks
Execution and risk management
Apply Agile methodologies to organize and manage sprints, supporting a streamlined and efficient development process within your team
Partner closely with Engineering to estimate scope and timelines, continuously refining plans as work progresses and new information emerges
Keep stakeholders informed of project status, proactively flagging risks or deviations from plan and proposing solutions rather than just surfacing problems
Drive product launches by ensuring that all relevant parts of the organization — Engineering, Operations, Sales, Marketing, and Support — are prepared and aligned
Analyze metrics post-launch to evaluate impact, identify gaps, and inform the next iteration of your roadmap
Travel up to 10% annually for team collaboration, customer research, and training
Desired Traits and Qualifications, Education and Experience Equivalency:
Past Experience:
2–4 years of product management experience, ideally in a B2B software, e-commerce, or platform environment
Demonstrated experience owning a defined product area from discovery through delivery — including writing requirements, managing scope, and tracking outcomes
Experience working closely with Engineering and Design teams in an Agile development environment
Track record of building productive working relationships with cross-functional stakeholders and earning credibility through clear communication and reliable execution
Experience using data and customer insights to inform prioritization decisions and evaluate the impact of product changes
Familiarity with defining and tracking product metrics — both leading indicators and business outcomes
Desired
Experience in one or more of the following domains: catalog and search, e-commerce platform, supply chain or order management, customer experience, or internal business systems
Exposure to platforms with large or complex catalogs, configurable products, or high-SKU-count inventory — where search relevance, attribute structure, and navigation design are meaningful product challenges
Familiarity with industrial manufacturing, hardware product development, or engineering procurement workflows — or a genuine interest in developing that knowledge quickly
Experience with operational tooling or business systems (e.g., ERP, CMS, CRM, PIM) and how they interact with customer-facing product experiences
Skills
Strong analytical skills: able to break high-level goals into actionable requirements by synthesizing data, customer insights, and stakeholder input to drive sound product decisions
Clear written and verbal communication: able to write crisp requirements and PRDs, facilitate productive cross-functional discussions, and give stakeholders the information they need to act
Structured thinking: approaches ambiguous problems with a clear process — defining the problem, gathering evidence, framing options, and making a reasoned recommendation
Results orientation: focused on outcomes and impact, not just completing tasks — takes ownership of the success of their work end to end
Collaborative working style: builds relationships across functions with empathy and accountability, and earns credibility through consistency and follow-through
Active and growing AI practice: uses AI tools as a genuine accelerant for drafting, research synthesis, and ideation — and demonstrates intellectual curiosity and learning velocity in developing new AI-assisted workflows as the tooling landscape evolves
Builder mindset: comfortable experimenting with AI-assisted prototyping to communicate product ideas, test assumptions, and accelerate the feedback loop — treating working artifacts as a complement to written documentation, not a replacement for it
Curiosity and learning agility: proactively seeks to understand the business, the customer, and the technical context — and applies new knowledge to improve their product decisions
Perks and Benefits
Competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance
401K plan
Parental leave programs
Paid volunteer days
And much, much more!

Excel at being part of a strong, empathetic team.
Thrive in an environment emphasizing respect, honesty, collaboration, and growth.

Help us continue to build a world-class organization that values the contributions of all of our teammates

title: Technical Program Manager
description:
Who we are:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the team:
Formic's Business Systems team builds and manages the software, data infrastructure, and integrations that power our operations.
Our work touches nearly every part of the company. We build internal applications that help teams manage robot deployments and field service, connect operational data across platforms, and develop AI-powered tools that make information more accessible and work more efficient. We also help shape the systems behind our sales, marketing, finance, and other business processes.
Some solutions are custom-built applications. Others involve integrating existing platforms, automating workflows, or rethinking how information moves through the business. We work directly with the people using these systems and own what we deliver, including adoption, reliability, and ongoing improvement.
We're a small team with significant autonomy, tackling technical challenges across a robotics company where the software we build has a direct impact on real-world operations.
About the role:
We're looking for a technically strong, AI-forward builder who can turn complex business problems into working software.
You'll work directly with teams across Formic to identify opportunities and build solutions, whether that's developing an internal application, connecting systems that don't communicate, automating an operational process, or applying AI to make existing tools more useful.
You'll have the autonomy to determine what to build and how to build it, along with responsibility for getting it into production and making sure it works. We want someone who moves quickly, makes sound technical decisions, and cares as much about adoption and reliability as development.
This isn't a traditional product management role or one focused exclusively on AI. It's a hands-on opportunity for someone who loves building software and wants to see the impact of their work.
We care more about what you've built than your job title or career path. You might come from software engineering, applied AI, technical product development, business systems engineering, or a startup where you've worn several hats. What matters is that you know how to turn ideas into working software and can show us what you've shipped.
In this role you will:
Build and maintain internal applications, AI-powered tools, automations, and integrations that solve problems across Formic
Work directly with employees and business leaders to understand existing processes, uncover inefficiencies, and determine what should be built
Design technical solutions, including application architecture, APIs, databases, data pipelines, and integrations with existing platforms
Experiment with LLMs, AI agents, and emerging development tools, applying them where they offer a meaningful advantage
Connect information across business systems to improve data quality, visibility, and decision-making
Take projects from initial discovery through prototyping, development, deployment, and ongoing support
Build with security, reliability, maintainability, and scalability in mind, including appropriate testing and monitoring
Gather feedback, measure adoption and results, and continuously improve the products you deliver
Collaborate with engineering and other technical teams when projects require shared infrastructure or specialized expertise
Help determine the priorities, architecture, and technical direction of our Business Systems function
What makes you a great fit:
A strong track record of personally building and shipping software, internal products, automations, or other technical solutions that people rely on
Solid software development skills, including experience working with APIs, databases, and modern application development tools
Proficiency in at least one modern programming language, such as Python or TypeScript, and experience working with APIs, databases, and SQL
Hands-on experience integrating systems and working with data across multiple platforms
Practical experience using AI in software development or building AI-powered applications, with genuine curiosity about emerging capabilities
The ability to make thoughtful technical decisions without overengineering solutions
Strong product instincts. You can understand what users need, distinguish symptoms from underlying problems, and prioritize work based on impact
Comfort working independently, navigating ambiguity, and owning projects from beginning to end
An appreciation for what happens after launch, including testing, documentation, monitoring, maintenance, and user adoption
The ability to communicate clearly with technical and nontechnical colleagues
A bias toward action, intellectual curiosity, and genuine interest in how businesses operate
Bonus points if you have:
Experience building with LLM APIs, AI agents, retrieval-augmented generation, or agentic workflows
Experience building and deploying cloud-based applications
Familiarity with CRM, ERP, finance, or operational systems and the data that connects them
Experience with workflow orchestration, event-driven integrations, or data engineering
Experience building applications that handle sensitive business information
A background in robotics, manufacturing, industrial automation, logistics, or field service operations.
Experience working in a startup or small technical team where you've had substantial ownership.
Our Total Rewards:
At Formic, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported both professionally and personally. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits and perks package for full-time, U.S.-based team members, including:
Equity in Formic: Participate in our stock option program and share in the success of a fast-growing start-up backed by leading global investors
Competitive & Uncapped Commission Structure: Designed to reward performance and impact in commission-eligible roles
Comprehensive Healthcare Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance through Blue Cross Blue Shield and Unum, with 99% of employee premiums covered and 75% coverage for dependents, with optional buy-up plans available
Additional Insurance Benefits: FSA and DCFSA, life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability through Unum, all 100% employer-paid
Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Fully funded by Formic, offering support when you need it most
Paid Parental Leave Program: Up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave
Company-sponsored 401(k): Invest in your future with our company-facilitated retirement savings plan
Home Office Stipend: A one-time allowance for fully remote and hybrid employees to support an at-home or on-the-road work setup
Monthly Cell Phone Reimbursement: Monthly stipend toward personal phone and internet expenses
Flexible Time Off: Take the time you need, when you need it, supported by our flexible PTO policy
Compensation Philosophy
Formic’s pay and equity packages are thoughtfully benchmarked against peer companies at a similar growth stage. Equity represents a meaningful part of our mutual investment: when Formic succeeds, so do you.
Final offers are customized based on experience, geographic location, market considerations, and a candidate’s preferred balance of cash and equity. Our goal is to attract and reward top talent who will have significant impact, and we are open to thoughtful discussions to align on the right structure.
Compensation Range: $135,000 — $175,000 USD What we look for:
We’re building this company from the ground up, and every person we hire has an outsized impact on our culture, performance, and trajectory. While each team member brings unique strengths and perspectives, we look for people who align with our Operating Principles and embody them in action. If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!
Fearless Optimism: You make bold bets and default optimistic. You believe in the mission, aren’t paralyzed by risk, and fear inaction more than failure. You see ambiguity as opportunity and bring energy to building what doesn’t yet exist.
Create the Magic: You absorb complexity so customers don’t have to. Whether your customer is external or internal, you focus on delivering experiences that are clear, fast, value-added, and outcome-driven. You don’t say “not my job.” You make things work.
Today, Not Tomorrow: You have a bias to action. You close the loop. You take extreme ownership. You understand that speed compounds, and you don’t confuse activity with results.
Seek Truth: You think from first principles. You value data over ego and strong opinions loosely held. You’re willing to challenge assumptions, including your own, in pursuit of the best answer.
Made of Rubber: You are resolute and adaptable. When things break or priorities shift, you rebound stronger. You treat setbacks as learning moments and move forward with grit.
One Formic: You operate without silos. You practice radical helpfulness, document clearly, and make clean handoffs. You assume positive intent and prioritize team success over individual credit.

We are seeking an experienced Security Manager to lead the governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) pillar of our Enterprise Cybersecurity program. This people-leadership role owns the cybersecurity governance operating rhythm, executive and board-level reporting, third-party security risk management, data security program management, security awareness, and cybersecurity policy and compliance activities. The Security Manager is accountable for the cadence, quality, and continuity of these programs — turning security metrics, risk data, and regulatory requirements into clear, actionable insight for leadership and the Board.
The ideal candidate combines strong program and people management with a solid understanding of security frameworks (such as NIST CSF and CMMC), risk management, and stakeholder engagement across IT, Legal, business units, and external partners. This role reports to the Sr. Dir, Enterprise Cyber Security and directly manages analysts supporting governance, risk, and awareness functions.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Cybersecurity Governance & Reporting
Own the cybersecurity governance program, including the Monthly Cybersecurity Metrics Report and Quarterly Board Dashboard measures.
Define and maintain cybersecurity metrics, KPIs, and KRIs; track program maturity against the NIST CSF; and drive strategic initiatives, risks, and governance commitments to closure.
Coordinate identity governance activities, including monthly AD account reviews, access certifications, and IAM metrics reporting.
Coordinate cybersecurity inputs for the annual cyber insurance renewal and annual Incident Response Plan update and Management tabletop exercise.
Data Security Program Management
Lead data discovery and classification governance across IT, Legal, and business stakeholders, tracking data risk reduction and reporting progress through program metrics.
Third-Party & Supplier Cyber Risk Management
Manage the third-party cyber risk assessment program, including new third-party service reviews, periodic reassessments, critical-supplier (direct and indirect) assessments, and FBIN questionnaires.
Track and drive remediation of third-party and supplier risks and integrate cyber-risk data into governance reporting.
Security Vendor Administration & Operational Oversight
Provide governance administration for cybersecurity vendors (PO creation, invoice processing, DocuSign workflows, renewal tracking) and support legal/contract activities such as NDA/MNDA reviews and security questionnaire responses.
Cybersecurity Policies, Standards & Compliance
Maintain cybersecurity governance documentation, coordinating annual policy and standard updates, approvals, publication and archive.
Support compliance initiatives including SOX controls, CMMC readiness, NIST CSF maturity reporting, SOC 2 assurance, and audit evidence collection and manage governance repositories and control attestations.
Security Awareness Program
Administer the enterprise security awareness program, including annual training, new hire training, National Cybersecurity Awareness Month, quarterly phishing simulations and ad hoc awareness articles on the FBIN intranet.
Leadership & Continuous Improvement
Manage, mentor, and develop analysts supporting governance, risk, and awareness functions.
Partner with cross-functional teams: IT, Legal, connected product, and business units to embed security best practices and continuously improve the maturity, efficiency, and clarity of processes and reporting.

Collaborate: Build partnerships and work collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives.
Communicate Effectively: Develop and deliver multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences.
Instill Trust: Gain the confidence and trust of others through honesty, integrity, and authenticity.
Builds Effective Teams: Attract, develop, and retain talent to meet current and future organizational needs.
Drives Results: Consistently achieve results, even under challenging circumstances.
Decision Quality: Make sound and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward.
Plans and Aligns: Plan and prioritize work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals.
Ensures Accountability: Hold self and others accountable to meet commitments.
Bachelor's degree in Information Security, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
Minimum of 7+ years of overall technology experience, with at least 5+ years in an information security, cybersecurity, or GRC role.
Demonstrated experience owning cybersecurity governance, risk, or compliance programs and producing executive- or board-level reporting.
Working knowledge of security frameworks such as NIST CSF and CMMC, and of enterprise risk and third-party risk management practices.
Experience coordinating security awareness, data security, or identity governance programs across cross-functional stakeholders.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex security topics for technical and non-technical audiences, including leadership.
Strong analytical, organizational, and program-management skills.
PREFERRED :
Prior people-leadership or team-management experience.
Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CISA, or CompTIA Security+.
Experience with GRC and risk platforms and data security tooling.

The Data Center team designs and operates some of the most sophisticated electrical engineering, mechanical engineering and HVAC systems in the world. Facilities Technicians at Google data centers operate, monitor and support physical facilities conditions. Some of these duties will include heating and cooling of air and water, power supply, generators, UPS systems, electrical distribution and control and monitoring systems. You regularly help inspect, maintain and repair various data center systems such as piping and non-critical electrical or mechanical system components). You provide daily assistance to senior technicians as you read blueprints/schematics, conduct tours of systems and assess their working order.

As a Facilities Technician, you will operate, monitor, and support physical facilities conditions for our data centers.

Basic Function
This position is responsible for supporting and improving CNC manufacturing processes and daily operations for new and existing products within assigned Business Units to optimize efficiency, quality, and performance. The Manufacturing Process Engineer will apply CNC machining expertise, CAD/CAM software knowledge, and CNC programming skills to develop, implement, and sustain robust manufacturing processes. This position utilizes the ITW toolbox to drive attainment of quality, cost, and delivery objectives while ensuring compliance with ISO 9001 quality system requirements.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Marginal position functions not included among the essential duties and responsibilities are also requirements of this position.
1. Develop and improve CNC manufacturing processes and process instructions (OMS) by studying product requirements; researching, designing, modifying, and validating manufacturing methods, tooling, fixtures, and equipment.
2. Create, modify, optimize, and troubleshoot CNC programs for milling, turning, and multi-axis machining operations using CAD/CAM software.
3. Support CNC machine setup, prove-out activities, tooling selection, cutting parameter optimization, and process validation to improve productivity and part quality.

9. Lead manufacturing readiness activities for new product introductions and production recommendations.
10. Analyze manufacturing performance data including yield, scrap, rework, cycle time, tool life, and machine utilization to identify and implement continuous improvement opportunities.
11. Review, communicate, and implement engineering change orders to sustain production, improve quality, reduce costs, and increase manufacturing efficiency.
12. Provide technical leadership and guidance to manufacturing technicians, CNC machinists, team leads, and operators.
13. Support Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and continuous improvement initiatives within the CNC machining environment.

· Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience programming CNC mills, lathes, or multi-axis machining centers.
· Experience using CAD/CAM software such as Mastercam, SolidWorks CAM, Fusion 360, Siemens NX, GibbsCAM, or similar manufacturing platforms.
· Strong knowledge of CNC machining practices, tooling, cutting parameters, GD&T, blueprint reading, and machining process development.

ITW Food Equipment Group LLC designs and manufactures commercial food equipment for food service and retail customers through its subsidiaries. The Service/Repair Technician 2 possesses fundamental knowledge and has demonstrated mechanical and electrical aptitude with troubleshooting experience. title: Third Shift Lead Process Technician
description:
Job Description:
ITW's Lakeville, CT facility is seeking an experienced 3rd Shift Lead Process Technician to join our manufacturing team.
We are a clean, modern, fully in-line, highly automated Automotive manufacturing facility utilizing state-of-the-art injection molding equipment, robotics, automated material handling, and advanced vision inspection systems.
The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience with plastic injection molding processes, injection mold tooling, and hot runner systems. Experience with automation and robotic systems is highly desirable.
This position will serve as the technical and operational lead for third-shift manufacturing, providing direction, supervision, and mentorship to machine operators while ensuring production requirements, quality standards, and equipment performance are consistently maintained.
The successful candidate must obtain strong communication skills, possess excellent mechanical aptitude, and demonstrate the ability to independently troubleshoot processing and equipment issues while effectively leading the production team.
This is a hands-on leadership position requiring a balance of technical process knowledge, equipment setup & troubleshooting, production oversight, and team leadership.
Key Responsibilities
Injection Molding Process & Equipment
Set up, start up, and optimize injection molding processes to meet production and quality requirements.
Monitor and maintain process parameters to ensure consistent part quality and production efficiency.
Troubleshoot injection molding process issues, including short shots, flash, dimensional variation, cosmetic defects, and other quality-related concerns.
Demonstrate a strong understanding of injection molds, mold construction, and hot runner systems.
Perform mold changes, process setups, and equipment adjustments as required.
Identify opportunities to improve cycle times, scrap reduction, and improve overall equipment performance.
Work closely with Engineering, Quality, and Maintenance to resolve process and equipment-related issues.
Ensure all production equipment is cleaned, maintained, operating safely and efficiently
Monitor and support Wittmann Battenfeld, Nissei & Toshiba injection molding machines.
Automation & Advanced Manufacturing Technology
Support the operation, setup, and troubleshooting of Wittmann robotic equipment.
Support Wittmann central material feeding systems and auxiliary equipment.
Monitor and troubleshoot automated material handling systems and associated equipment.
Support and troubleshoot Keyence vision inspection systems used to identify part defects and quality-related issues.
Ensure automated inspection systems are functioning properly and identify potential quality concerns.
Work with Maintenance and Engineering to resolve molding & automation-related downtime and equipment issues.
Third Shift Leadership & Production Support
Serve as the technical and operational lead for third-shift manufacturing operations.
Supervise, direct, and mentor machine operators to ensure production expectations are met.
Provide technical guidance and support to operators when processing or equipment issues arise.
Monitor production performance, scrap, downtime, and overall shift efficiency.
Ensure operators follow established work instructions, quality requirements, and safety procedures.
Communicate production concerns, equipment issues, quality problems, and outstanding maintenance needs to the appropriate personnel and incoming shifts.
Maintain accurate production records shift end emails and shift reports.
Escalate issues appropriately and ensure timely resolution of production concerns.
Promote accountability, teamwork, and a positive working environment.
Communication & Documentation
Maintain strong communication with production leadership, Engineering, Quality, Maintenance, and other departments.
Provide detailed and accurate shift handoff information to ensure production continuity.
Utilize Microsoft Office applications, including Excel and Word, for production documentation and reporting.
Utilize Microsoft Outlook for professional communication and coordination.
Maintain accurate records of production issues, downtime. scrap, and process changes.
Additional Responsibilities
Perform other related duties and responsibilities as assigned to support manufacturing operations and business needs.
Required Qualifications
Previous 5+ years' experience as a Process Technician in a plastic injection molding manufacturing environment.
Strong understanding of injection molding processes and process optimization.
Experience working with injection molds and hot runner systems.
Demonstrated troubleshooting skills involving molding processes, equipment, and quality-related issues.
Ability to identify and resolve processing issues independently.
Strong mechanical aptitude and hands-on troubleshooting abilities.
Previous experience providing technical direction, leading, supervising, or mentoring production personnel.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

coordinating all international movements originating from the United States to destinations
worldwide, including but not limited to Mexico, Germany, Bulgaria, and Malaysia. The scope
includes equipment, service parts, repairs, upgrades, returns, loaners, demonstrations,
manufacturing-related tools, components, and materials. This role serves as the primary
coordinator for the end-to-end Shipment Authorization Form (SAF) process and as the

customs brokers, suppliers, and trade compliance. The position owns shipment visibility,
status management, escalation handling, regulatory readiness, classification
governance, permit management, and export/import compliance from submission through
U.S. export and destination-country import. It ensures products are properly classified,
registered, documented, and compliance-ready before shipment approval.

 Manage end-to-end international movements of capital equipment, repairs, returns,
demonstration units, components, service parts, manufacturing-related tools, and
materials from the United States to countries worldwide

United States and related returns, and lead cross-functional escalation calls for critical
shipments.

milestones and readiness, and serve as the primary owner of the SAF Helpline Zoom
Channel.
 Provide shipment status updates to engineers and project teams, track open issues,
and ensure timely resolution.
 Coordinate with customs brokers, freight forwarders, and logistics providers to
support timely U.S. export and destination-country import clearance and resolve holds,
delays, documentation issues, and classification discrepancies.
 Manage U.S. export and destination-country tariff classification activities.
 Partner with engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, suppliers, and
trade compliance to obtain and evaluate technical information required for classification
and country of origin determinations.

materials, component information, and product functionality to support HTS, Schedule
B, ECCN, and country of origin determinations.
 Verify completion of classification, country of origin documentation, FTA eligibility, metal
certificates, permit or license approvals, and customs documentation readiness.
 Evaluate destination-country import requirements, including permits, product
registrations, labeling or conformity requirements, special regulations, and customs
restrictions.
 Coordinate product data required for applicable customs, inventory control, and trade
compliance systems.
 Ensure products are compliance-ready before shipment authorization and support
inventory registration requirements and customs record maintenance.
 Ensure accurate tracking of exported, imported, transformed, returned, scrapped, and
transferred goods.
 Prepare, review, and validate commercial invoices, export filings, permits, licenses,
certificates, temporary import/export documents, and country-specific customs
declarations.
 Ensure compliance with U.S. export requirements, destination-country import
regulations, applicable trade laws, sanctions and restricted-party requirements, and
company policies.
 Maintain complete, audit-ready trade records and ensure proper export documentation,
recordkeeping, and regulatory compliance.
 Support engineering, manufacturing, service, and supply chain teams with global trade
compliance requirements.
 Support tariff and export classification, country of origin determinations, and trade
program utilization.
 Participate in internal audits and government compliance reviews, perform trade
compliance due diligence and transaction reviews, and support audits and
investigations.
 Identify compliance risks, implement corrective actions, and define requirements for
new shipment types and destination countries.
 Develop and maintain SOPs, procedures, work instructions, playbooks, knowledge
repositories, and classification databases.
 Identify process improvement and automation opportunities and support
implementation of global trade technology solutions.
 Maintain SAF tracking dashboards and monitor SLA performance; report shipment
aging, cycle times, backlog, and escalation metrics.
 Perform other duties, tasks, and special projects as assigned.

 Minimum 5 years of experience in:
• U.S.-Mexico cross-border operations
• Customs compliance
• Import/export operations
• IMMEX program administration
 Experience preparing customs documentation and supporting customs audits.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Advanced Excel and ERP system experience.
 Fluent in English and Spanish (written and verbal).
Preferred Skills and Experience
 Experience in the medical device, healthcare, pharmaceutical, or highly regulated
manufacturing industry.
 Experience with FDA-regulated products.
 Knowledge of USMCA and other free trade agreement requirements.
 Experience with SAP, GTS, Annex 24 software, or other customs compliance systems.
 Customs certifications or trade compliance credentials are a plus.
 Knowledge of:
• IMMEX Program
• Annex 24
• Annex 30
• U.S. Import Compliance
• U.S. Export Compliance
• Customs broker management
• Temporary import/export programs
Education & Training
 Bachelor's degree in engineering, international trade, customs administration, supply
chain, business, logistics, or a related field.

Normal office conditions.
Travel required (<10%) – both domestic and international.

title: Director Enterprise Learning
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
The opportunity:
Advancing minimally invasive care requires more than great technology — it requires people who grow with the company, lead with intention, and bring their best to every challenge. The Director, Enterprise Learning will shape how we build capability from the inside out: ensuring every employee, manager, and director has the knowledge, skills, and mindset to perform and grow.
We're looking for someone who sees learning as a business discipline, not a support function. Someone who starts with strategy — understanding where Intuitive is headed and what capabilities will get us there — and works backward to design learning that actually moves the needle. A builder who combines learning design expertise with sharp business judgment, and who knows how to measure whether any of it is working.
This role covers role agnostic enterprise learning below the VP level: individual contributor development, manager learning, director learning, and employee onboarding. It's a broad remit that requires both vision and execution — and a leader who can do both.
What you'll lead:
You'll report directly to the VP, Global Talent and own the strategy, design, and delivery of enterprise-wide learning programs that are connected to business priorities, deliver measurable impact, and built to last. This isn't about building a curriculum library — it's about building capability that shows up in business results.
What this looks like:
Anchor learning to business strategy. Partner closely with HR Business Partners, business leaders, and the broader Talent team to understand where the company is going and what capabilities will be required to get there. Translate that into a multi-year enterprise learning strategy with clear priorities, measurable outcomes, and a coherent point of view on what we build, buy, or curate.
Design learning that works. Lead the design and delivery of learning experiences across the full employee population — from onboarding through director-level development. Apply modern instructional design principles across a range of modalities: in-person, digital, cohort-based, on-demand, and AI-enabled. Prioritize approaches that fit how people actually learn at work.
Own manager and director development. Build and continuously evolve learning programs for managers and directors that are practical, relevant, and grounded in what Intuitive needs from its people leaders. Work closely with HR Business Partners to ensure programs address real capability gaps, not just generic leadership topics.
Deliver a best-in-class onboarding experience. Design and steward an onboarding experience that accelerates time-to-productivity, connects new employees to Intuitive's mission and culture, and sets a strong foundation for long-term engagement and performance.
Make learning measurable. Define clear success metrics for every major program and build the infrastructure to track them. Move beyond attendance and satisfaction scores — connect learning outcomes to performance, retention, and business impact. Use data to make honest calls about what's working and what isn't.
Bring modern learning approaches to life. Stay close to how the learning landscape is evolving — AI-enabled personalization, digital learning platforms, cohort learning, nudge-based reinforcement — and bring the right innovations into Intuitive in ways that are practical and scalable, not just novel.
Build and lead a high-performing team. Lead a team of learning professionals with clarity, high standards, and genuine investment in their development. Create an environment where craft matters, outcomes are tracked, and continuous improvement is the norm.
Partner across HR and the business. Work closely with Talent Management, HR Business Partners, People Analytics, and I&D to ensure enterprise learning is integrated into the broader talent strategy — and that programs reflect and reinforce an inclusive, high-performance culture.
Design and lead manager enablement strategies and programs that equip leaders with the tools, resources, and capabilities to effectively lead and develop their teams.
Design and lead AI enablement and literacy initiatives that build employee confidence, accelerate responsible adoption, and help teams effectively integrate AI into their day-to-day work.
Qualifications
What you'll bring:
Learning strategy and design expertise: Significant experience designing and delivering enterprise learning programs across multiple audiences and modalities — from onboarding through senior individual contributors and people leaders. You understand instructional design deeply and apply it with both rigor and pragmatism.
Business acumen: You think like a business leader. You understand how Intuitive creates value, what's driving the strategy, and how to connect learning investments to business outcomes. You can hold your own in conversations with senior leaders about priorities, trade-offs, and ROI.
Modern learning fluency: Genuine familiarity with the evolving learning landscape — AI-enabled learning tools, digital platforms, cohort-based models, on-demand content strategies, and data-driven personalization. You know what's worth adopting and how to bring it in thoughtfully.
Measurement and outcomes orientation: A track record of defining meaningful success metrics for learning programs and using data to drive decisions. You're not satisfied with completion rates — you want to know whether learning changed behavior and moved business results.
Stakeholder influence: Strong ability to build relationships with and influence senior business leaders and HR partners. You can translate learning strategy into language that resonates with business audiences, and you earn credibility through follow-through and results.
People leadership: You lead with clarity and high standards, invest genuinely in your team's growth, and create an environment where excellent work is the expectation.
Operational excellence: You can manage a complex portfolio of programs, vendors, and priorities without losing sight of quality. You build systems and processes that scale — and you know when to simplify.
Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree in Learning & Development, Organizational Psychology, Instructional Design, or a related field preferred.
12+ years of progressive experience in enterprise learning, with demonstrated success leading learning strategy and design across a large, complex organization.
Experience with AI-enabled learning tools and modern digital learning platforms strongly preferred.
Ability to travel approximately 20% of the time.

This role combines the judgment and executive partnership of a chief of staff with the discipline of a portfolio program manager and the ownership of a hands-on operator.

title: Director, Internal Controls
description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.
Invenergy follows a hybrid schedule, working in office Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays if work permits.
This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.
Job Description
Position Overview
The Director of Internal Controls will build and lead a practical, business-focused enterprise internal control and risk management program that supports Invenergy’s continued growth. This role will partner directly with leaders across finance, accounting, technology, legal, compliance, development, construction, and operations to identify and assess significant risks, establish scalable controls, strengthen process documentation, and promote clear ownership and accountability.
The Director will be a hands-on leader who can set the strategy, develop the program, and work alongside the business to provide practical, risk-based guidance and maintain an effective, sustainable control environment as the organization evolves.
Responsibilities
Build and lead a formal annual enterprise risk assessment process that identifies significant risks across the organization, evaluates their relative likelihood and impact, and maps the controls intended to mitigate those risks.
Incorporate fraud risk into the annual assessment, including potential fraud schemes, incentives and opportunities, management override, and the preventive and detective controls needed to address those risks.
Maintain a practical, formally documented risk and internal control inventory that identifies each objective, associated risk, control activity, owner, and frequency, and ensure it is updated as the business, systems, risks, and processes change.
Ensure key processes and controls are supported by approved, usable procedures that define the control objective, execution steps, frequency, preparer, reviewer, exception handling, escalation, and required evidence.
Develop a scalable internal control framework and operating model that reflects Invenergy’s ownership structure, business complexity, growth plans, and risk profile.
Work directly with business and functional leaders to establish clear accountability and design controls that are effective, efficient, and integrated into day-to-day operations.
Perform and oversee periodic reviews of control design and operation, identify gaps, agree on practical corrective actions with management, and monitor remediation through completion.
Challenge existing processes constructively and identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, and strengthen controls while supporting speed, accountability, and business growth.
Establish and maintain formal internal audit procedures, including a risk-based annual audit plan, scoping, planning, fieldwork, sampling, testing, documentation, quality review, reporting, issue rating, management responses, remediation follow-up, and escalation.
Maintain appropriate independence and objectivity for internal audit activities and coordinate efficiently with external auditors, legal, compliance, technology, and other assurance partners.

The EHS Manager will be responsible for the execution of the EHS strategy, culture and performance, overseeing Operational Risk Management (ORM) processes that include Safety and Health, Environment, Business Continuity, Facility Security, Asset Conservation, Department of Transportation (DOT) and Pandemic Planning. The primary purpose of this position is to ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state and local laws and regulations, and to ensure KraftHeinz EHS policies/procedures and processes are understood and sustained across the plant by employees, visitors and contractors. Own and execute EHS strategies that align with corporate objectives and aspirations

Job Description
Job Purpose
The R&D Scientist for Data Analytics & Operations uses R&D-owned data and technical knowledge to deliver accurate, actionable analysis that supports business decisions across business areas such as carbon accounting, nutrient profiling and compliance reporting, including Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR). This position keeps that data accurate, consistent, traceable and accessible for use across enterprise systems and digital solutions through stewardship, governance and documentation, and helps prepare it for use in a variety of digital tools and solutions. Working with regular guidance alongside Procurement, Corporate ESG, digital and other partners, the role represents North America R&D in enterprise sustainability and compliance initiatives, serving as a trusted link between R&D subject-matter expertise and cross-functional teams. It suits data professionals with food or CPG experience as well as food or packaging scientists with strong data skills.
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
​​Steward R&D data by investigating data-quality issues, reconciling discrepancies and keeping data accurate, consistent, and reliable across sources.
​Support data governance by applying established standards and maintaining definitions, mappings, taxonomy, metadata, validation checks and traceable documentation, flagging gaps to data owners
​Help prepare, structure and validate R&D data and content for ingestion into enterprise data platforms and downstream applications
​Query, combine and analyze R&D-owned product, ingredient, packaging and nutrition data to identify trends and deliver recurring reporting and analysis, for example carbon accounting, nutrient profiling and compliance reporting such as EPR
​Provide business requirements and validation criteria for automated, self-service and AI-enabled data solutions, and support testing for accuracy and relevance
​Use analytics to assess the impact of ingredient, packaging, specification or process changes across the portfolio by identifying affected products, technical dependencies and information gaps
​Participate in organizational sustainability and compliance initiatives, such as emissions-reduction and packaging programs, on behalf of North America R&D, contributing technical input and gathering information from R&D colleagues
​Collaborate with a wide range of cross-functional teams, support the use of relevant tools, data and guidance, and translate complex information for technical and non-technical partners ​
Manage multiple assignments across topic areas with regular guidance, moving between broad coverage and focused analysis as assignments require, prioritizing deliverables and escalating questions, risks and issues appropriately
Expected Experience & Required Skills
​​Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Food Science, Packaging, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Science, Agricultural Science, Nutrition, Data Science or a related field, or equivalent experience
​Minimum of two (2) years of relevant experience, or one (1) year with a Master’s degree, in data analysis, stewardship or reporting in a food, consumer packaged goods (CPG) or other regulated-product setting, or in food science, R&D or technical work with hands-on data analysis (post-graduation internship and co-op experience counts ).
​Proficiency in Excel and structured data analysis; SQL strongly preferred, or equivalent experience with tools such as Python or R.
​Working familiarity with R&D product, ingredient, packaging and nutrition data, and exposure to areas such as carbon accounting, nutrient profiling or regulatory reporting, including EPR.
​Learning agility, with a track record of quickly building expertise in new technical areas.
​Strong attention to detail and a commitment to data accuracy, validation and documentation.
​Effective communication, project management and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify discrepancies, interpret findings and explain data findings to non-technical partners.
​Experience with Power BI or Power Platform, or familiarity with AI tools and with information and knowledge management concepts such as data governance, data stewardship, taxonomy and metadata.
​Ability to manage competing priorities and work collaboratively, with curiosity, sound judgment and a self-starter mindset.
​Willingness to travel up to 10%, with additional travel possible depending on location and business needs.

As the Business Planner, Azure Container Services and Developer Innovation , you will play a critical role in shaping how Microsoft monetizes and grows some of Azure’s most important container, developer, and emerging AI services.
AI agents are moving from pilot to production, and they need a secure, scalable place to run. On Azure, that place is increasingly containers. This role puts you at the center of that shift: you will shape the business model for the container services that form the foundation for enterprise AI, and you will incubate new products from a blank page.
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is Azure's managed Kubernetes platform, widely adopted by enterprises to run applications at scale, and it is increasingly central to how organizations run AI workloads. You will own planning, pricing, and packaging across AKS Edge, ACI, and Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO), a fully managed OpenShift application platform for enterprises modernizing on Kubernetes. You will also lead Azure App Testing, Microsoft's unified testing platform that brings Load Testing, Playwright Testing, and other testing services together under one brand, spanning performance and functional testing. It is a high-growth, developer-centric market, with the global software testing market projected to exceed $500B by 2033, and you will shape pricing, packaging, and adoption to position Azure as the go-to platform for AI and intelligent application quality. Alongside it, you will incubate early-stage, emerging products, where you define the business model from concept to launch and decide what to scale, pivot, or stop.

You will partner directly with engineering, product, finance, marketing, sales, and pricing operations, while running an established portfolio and building what comes next.

A Microsoft Construction Quality Manager is responsible for governing the quality management system, auditing contractor quality performance, managing NCRs and quality metrics, identifying risks before they impact commissioning or operations, and ensuring data centers are delivered ready to perform—not just ready to complete.
Responsibilities
Core Responsibilities of a Microsoft Construction Quality Manager
1. Drive Construction Quality from Day One
Ensure facilities are built in accordance with design requirements, specifications, and Microsoft quality standards.
Promote a "Right First Time" culture to reduce rework, delays, and operational risks.
2. Audit Contractor Quality Programs
Verify General Contractors are executing their Quality Management System (QMS).
Conduct routine quality audits, inspections, and field observations.
Validate contractor compliance with Division 01 requirements, quality plans, inspection processes, and documentation requirements.
3. Manage NCRs and Quality Issues
Initiate and manage Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs).
Ensure corrective actions are developed, implemented, and verified.
Escalate unresolved quality issues to project leadership.
Trend recurring quality problems and drive systemic corrective actions.
4. Quality Management System Ownership
Establish and maintain project quality plans.
Review and align contractor quality plans before mobilization.
Standardize quality processes across projects and campuses.
5. Inspection & Test Planning Governance
Govern Inspection & Test Plans (ITPs).
Define hold points, quality gates, and documentation requirements.
Ensure Installer Verification Checklists (IVCs) and readiness requirements are met before commissioning milestones.
6. Digital Quality Platform Management
Administer quality tracking systems (Nexus/ACMS).
Monitor issue closure timelines and SLA performance.
Produce dashboards and quality metrics for leadership visibility.
7. Field Quality Assurance
Perform field inspections and observations.
Monitor workmanship trends and installation quality.
Verify contractors are following approved procedures and specifications.
Provide early identification of risks that could impact commissioning, IST, or turnover.
8. Readiness and Turnover Support
Support energization and commissioning readiness reviews.
Ensure documentation, inspections, punch lists, and quality issues are appropriately closed prior to turnover.
Partner with Commissioning Managers and Operations to improve startup outcomes.
9. Continuous Improvement
Analyze trends across campuses and metros.
Capture lessons learned.
Recommend process improvements that improve quality performance and reduce recurrence of defects.
10. Contractor Accountability
Hold GCs accountable for their QA/QC responsibilities.
Monitor closure performance and response times.
Reinforce that workmanship quality remains the responsibility of the contractor. Microsoft Quality provides oversight and assurance.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree in Construction Project Management, Architecture, Engineering, or related field AND 5+ years related experience OR equivalent experience.
Preferred Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree in Construction Project Management, Architecture, Engineering, or related field AND 8+ years related experience OR equivalent experience.
7+ years experience working on data center projects.
Proficient in data analytics, reporting, and construction management tools such as Power BI, Nexus, Bluebeam, and BIM with strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Detail-oriented with strong knowledge of construction specifications, quality standards, and installation compliance requirements.
Experience with continuous improvement methodologies such as Lean, DMAIC, Six Sigma, and change management.
Experience applying structured problem-solving tools such as RCA, FMEA, 8D, and CAPA.
Knowledge of ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems, quality auditing, and Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) principles.
Experience developing, implementing, and managing structured quality management systems.
Professional quality certifications preferred, including USACE CQM, OSHA 30, ASQ CQE, CQA, CMQ/OE, Six Sigma Green Belt/Black Belt, ISO 9001 Lead Auditor, or equivalent.
Experience in data center, mission-critical, industrial, semiconductor, pharmaceutical, power, or oil & gas construction environments preferred.
Other Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings.

title: Critical Environment Technician (Night Shift)
description:

As a  Critical Environment Technician (CET)  in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will help to maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our datacenters up and running. This could be anything from performing basic monitoring and inspection, performing various types of maintenance, participating in equipment troubleshooting, enforcing all safety and security requirements, and developing methods of operating procedures (MOPs) and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
Performs troubleshooting of equipment and systems independently within their trained discipline(s). Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Communicates and/or escalates troubleshooting issues or anomalies with assistance from more experienced colleagues. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained.
Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for appropriately leveled procedures to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments.
Develops an understanding of method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.
Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs (e.g., basic replacements, changing of parts) for specific disciplines and equipment for which they have been trained, following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs lower level maintenance with minimal supervision, and may resolve high level issues with support from more experienced colleagues. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance.
Equipment and Systems Operations Safely responds to and stabilizes abnormal conditions within the required timeframes for various abnormal facility events within data center with minimal supervision, utilizing emergency operating procedures (EOPs). Gathers necessary information and participates in the creation of incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Assists in developing emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Assists in providing emergency monitoring response to irregular or malfunctioning conditions.
Works on tasks (e.g., making rounds, initial assessments on equipment performance) as assigned with varying levels of supervision, sometime minimal. Supports senior colleagues as an assistant. Builds knowledge in operating equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls). Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
Performs monitoring physical inspection of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify critical alarms. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems.
Physical Requirements Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting 50lbs / 22.5kg. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg. with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Working Conditions Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
As indicated above, this role has a travel requirement of up to 25% which means you may be required to travel, from time to time, as part of this role.
As indicated above,   have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Other
Embodies our  culture  and  values .

High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent.

Associate's Degree or technical trade certification (e.g., military, trade school), or higher-equivalent education OR High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent AND 1+ year(s) technical services experience (e.g., high-availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical)

title: Director, Volume Licensing Programs Modernization
description:
Overview
About Monetization Strategy & Licensing (MSL)
Monetization Strategy & Licensing (MSL) is a newly formed organization at the core of Microsoft's Business strategy. MSL brings together the teams that decide how Microsoft prices, packages, and monetizes its commercial products, together with the licensing programs and partner agreements that carry that commercial model to market.
The organization was established as Microsoft enters its next phase of AI-driven transformation, when customer expectations and commercial models are shifting faster than ever. MSL's charter is to modernize the commercial engine beneath that shift: evolving legacy licensing constructs toward cloud- and consumption-based models, growing multi-billion-dollar revenue streams, and keeping Microsoft's programs both compliant and competitive across a complex global regulatory landscape.
Role Overview
The Director, Volume Licensing Programs Modernization leads the modernization of Microsoft's legacy Volume Licensing (VL) programs: the Microsoft Products & Services Agreement (MPSA), Select and Select Plus, and the Open family of programs (Open License, Open Value, and Open Value Subscription). These programs were designed for a perpetual-license, on-premises world. As customer needs shift to cloud and consumption, this role will shape how they evolve alongside Microsoft’s modern commerce motions.
This role owns the strategy to evolve these programs and guide customers and partners toward CSP, MCA-E, and Web Direct, while preserving revenue, protecting customers with legitimate perpetual-licensing needs, and minimizing disruption to partners and channels. The successful candidate will operate with significant independence, lead complex cross-group work as an individual contributor, influencing without direct authority across finance, commerce, engineering, CELA, partner, and field teams, and bring well-framed, data-driven options to senior leadership.
Responsibilities
Strategic Programs You Will Modernize / Key Responsibilities
This role modernizes a set of long-lived, high-revenue programs that are central to Microsoft's shift toward subscription and cloud-based commerce:
Legacy VL Program Strategy and Roadmap
Own the end-to-end strategy for MPSA, Select / Select Plus, and Open Value / Open Value Subscription. This includes building the diagnostic fact base on legacy program growth dynamics and EA-to-legacy migration patterns, evaluating future-state options and ensuring customers with specialized needs  (public sector, regulated procurement, air-gapped, and long-lifecycle scenarios).
Modern Commerce Motion Transition
Design structured migration paths that move legacy VL customers and partners to CSP, MCA-E, and Web Direct while preserving customer relationships and revenue. Drive the business requirements for the modern-commerce capabilities this transition depends on, including perpetual-licensing support, indirect resell, and public sector constructs in MCA-E. Lead the opportunity to evolve transactional license sales in favor of subscription, to which MPSA, Select, and Open are major contributors.
Price Optimization and Revenue Yield
Drive pricing and program strategy across the legacy VL portfolio, using pricing, product, and partner levers together to deliver customer value and support the move to modern commerce. Bring the analytical rigor to scenario-plan and quantify the revenue, customer, and partner impact of every pricing and program action before it ships, across commercial, government, education, and non-profit segments.
Program Integrity, Compliance and Regulatory Risk
Keep legacy programs compliant while they remain in market. Partner with legal, risk, and engineering teams to strengthen program integrity while preserving legitimate customer pathways. Navigate anti-competition, transferability, and data-sovereignty considerations across geographies, applying geo-segmented treatment for international markets where appropriate.
Leadership Responsibilities
Lead large, cross-group virtual teams without direct authority, spanning finance, commerce, engineering, CELA, partner, and field organizations, through a dependency-driven, iterative strategy that keeps workstreams aligned and decisions moving.
Represent the work at leadership levels within and external to the company, bringing well-framed options and recommendations to senior stakeholders.
Partner with external partners and internal product, engineering, finance, field, CELA, and partner teams to land changes with minimal market disruption.
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree in Engineering/Computer Science, Economics, Business, or related field AND 6+ years product management, strategy consulting, finance, business/corporate development, or related experience OR equivalent experience.
Additional or preferred qualifications:
Substantial experience (typically 5+ years) in commercial licensing, volume licensing programs, pricing, or partner-program strategy, with deep subject-matter expertise in Microsoft's volume licensing and modern commerce models (CSP, MCA-E, Web Direct).
Proven command of pricing and business-model strategy, and the analytical discipline to quantify the impact of pricing and program decisions.
Experience leading large-scale program transitions, including customer, partner, and channel change management.
Familiarity with public sector and regulated procurement requirements, and with the legal and regulatory considerations that shape licensing program changes across geographies.
Demonstrated ability to lead through ambiguity and influence without authority across finance, commerce, engineering, legal, partner, and sales organizations.
Direct, credible written and verbal communication and the independence to bring well-framed options to senior stakeholders at the company.
