This role brings together product design, interaction design, animation, AI, storytelling, and software development. You will explore emerging technologies, experiment with new forms of human–AI interaction, and develop prototypes, tools, and reusable systems that help move ideas from early exploration toward real product experiences.
The ideal candidate is as comfortable imagining new product possibilities and crafting intuitive, expressive experiences as writing code, connecting systems, and debugging prototypes. You should bring deep expertise in at least one discipline and a demonstrated ability to bridge creative thinking and technical execution.
The future of Copilot and AI must be experienced, not just imagined. From entirely new product ideas, features, and interactions to embodied AI characters and how they move, speak, behave, and respond, the most compelling possibilities come to life through tangible, interactive experiences that people can see, feel, and explore.
You will help build the Creative Studio’s ability to imagine, prototype, validate, and bring these ideas to life—connecting creative strategy, design, storytelling, and emerging technologies to new product possibilities, strengthening shared technical capabilities, and bridging the gap between creative vision and implementation.
Responsibilities
Develop and prototype future AI experiences. Translate blue-sky Copilot and AI product ideas, narratives, and creative concepts into compelling UI explorations, UX flows, interactive demos, and working prototypes that advance the product experience, brand, identity, and creative vision.
Design embodied AI characters and experiences. Shape character identity, visual language, motion, expression, personality, and behavior across products and platforms, including onboarding, customization, voice, and feedback systems that make AI experiences intuitive, expressive, and trustworthy.
Build interactive, real-time systems. Develop, debug, and optimize character animation, input, and response systems, connecting UI frameworks such as React, real-time rendering technologies such as Babylon.js, and AI services into cohesive, performant experiences across platforms, including mobile.
Prototype with AI agents and emerging technologies. Experiment with conversational, multimodal, generative, and multi-agent systems, integrating models, tools, and services to coordinate actions, manage state, and explore new ways people interact with AI.
Bridge creative vision and engineering execution. Build everything from lightweight experiments to production-minded prototypes, working within established code architectures and engineering frameworks to develop maintainable, reusable components and evaluate technical feasibility.
Collaborate, validate, and scale ideas. Partner with Research, Design, Product, and Engineering to test tension, trust, and emotional response, refine concepts, and develop shared tools, workflows, and design patterns that accelerate creative exploration and implementation across the studio.

Master's Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Graphic Design, Product Design, Visual Design, Human Computer Interaction, or related field AND 3+ years experience working in product or service design and/or shipping production code

title: Senior Critical Environment Technician (Night Shift)
description:
Overview
As a Senior Critical Environment Technician (CET) in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our Datacenters up and running. This could be anything from coordinating with supplier/vendors, working closely with Management to address operational, risk and safety situations, mentoring other CE Technicians, having a hands-on understanding on how critical environment equipment works, performing various types of maintenance, responding to onsite incidents while coordinating with other critical facilities professionals, and using telemetry and other platforms to monitor equipment performance and operations.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
May travel up to 25%, typically domestically for training and/or supporting another site. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance
Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
Performs troubleshooting of equipment and systems independently within their trained discipline(s). Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Communicates and/or escalates troubleshooting issues or anomalies with assistance from more experienced colleagues. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained.

Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs lower level maintenance with minimal supervision, and may resolve high level issues with support from more experienced colleagues. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance.
Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for appropriately leveled procedures to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments.
Develops an understanding of method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.

Works on tasks (e.g., making rounds, initial assessments on equipment performance) as assigned with varying levels of supervision, sometimes minimal. Supports senior colleagues as an assistant. Builds knowledge in operating equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls). Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.

Gathers necessary information and participates in the creation of incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Assists in developing emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Assists in providing emergency monitoring response to irregular or malfunctioning conditions.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.

As a  Microsoft Senior Logistics Technician (Locations: Cartersville, GA), you will prioritize and assign ticketed work to technicians on the team, provide guidance on inbound/outbound logistics tasks, and ensure that inventory balances are accurate. This opportunity will allow you to demonstrate your expertise in standard processes and procedures for Inventory & Asset Management and develop skills around mentorship of peer technicians accelerating your career growth in the process.   Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.   Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 Data Centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.   With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.   Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.   In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.    Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Customer Service
Maintains a strong focus to understand the impact of their work when completing tickets and assigned Inventory and Asset Management (IAM) tasks. Communicates across Data Center teams (e.g., Site Services, Critical Environment, Facility Management, Security, Vendors, Safety, Supply Chain), and supports Microsoft and non-Microsoft gear deliveries. Inbound and Outbound Logistics

Documents inbound/outbound packages. Receives, confirms, tracks, stores, dispatches, and delivers material from the warehouse to destinations, including production facilities, retail stores, and corporate offices. Begins to communicate directly with customers, stakeholders, vendors, (e.g., landlords) in regard to scheduling both inbound and outbound deliveries. Applies appropriate customs documentations and standards for outbound packages. Ensures complete and detailed physical inventory tracking and staging.

Procurement

Safety Practices

Engages in Task Hazard Analysis (THA) consistently for every task to be performed and ensures sign off from appropriate person for any related risks. title: Sr Technical Program Manager
description:
Overview
Would you like to shape how Microsoft identifies, prioritizes, and reduces security and compliance risk across a complex, global business?   The Trust & Integrity Protection (TrIP) organization is seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager with a strong governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) background to lead a portfolio of security risk and mitigation programs. The successful candidate will translate complex regulatory, security, and policy requirements into actionable operating plans, controls, and executive decisions, and will drive risk identification, prioritization, and remediation at enterprise scale.   In this role, the candidate will work broadly across organizational boundaries, partnering with security, privacy, legal, compliance, engineering, and business teams, and engaging at both the executive and operational levels. The ideal candidate combines senior program management expertise with deep GRC experience, sound risk judgment, and the ability to turn ambiguity into clear plans and accountable outcomes.
Responsibilities
Lead the GRC security program portfolio. Own an integrated portfolio of security, compliance, and risk programs, setting priorities, sequencing mitigation efforts, and managing dependencies, milestones, and outcomes across multiple organizations.
Identify and prioritize risk. Drive risk identification, assessment, and prioritization across security, regulatory, and operational risk domains, applying consistent criteria to focus investment on the highest-impact exposures.
Drive action plans to closure. Translate prioritized risks into owned action plans with clear accountability, milestones, and success measures, and track remediation through to verified closure and evidence of control effectiveness.
Translate requirements into operating plans and controls. Convert complex regulatory, policy, contractual, and security requirements into practical operating plans, control designs, and implementation roadmaps that engineering and business teams can execute.
Enable executive decisions. Frame risk trade-offs, options, and recommendations for senior leaders, and prepare decision-ready briefings, executive summaries, and governance reviews that drive timely, accountable decisions.
Partner across risk disciplines. Work closely with Legal, Privacy, Compliance, Security, Internal Audit, and enterprise risk teams to align on obligations, shared controls, and coordinated responses, reducing duplication and closing gaps.
Establish governance and rhythm of business. Define and run governance forums, decision rights, escalation paths, metrics, and reporting cadences that provide transparency into risk posture and program health.
Lead across organizational boundaries. Build alignment and drive execution with engineering, operations, finance, and business leaders without direct authority, operating effectively at both the executive and operational levels.
Measure and continuously improve. Define meaningful risk and compliance metrics, and use data, automation, and AI-enabled tooling to improve control monitoring, reporting, and the overall operating model.

title: Deal Operations, AMER
description:
About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a senior individual contributor to support revenue growth across the Americas (AMER) by helping sales teams structure and close commercially sound deals. You will balance speed and responsiveness with pricing discipline, consistent processes, and appropriate financial and commercial controls.

In this role, you will be the day-to-day Deal Operations partner for AMER account teams, reviewing pricing, discounts, and commercial terms across new business, renewals, and expansions. You will guide sellers through deal requirements, evaluate non-standard requests, and coordinate the approvals needed to move opportunities through contracting and closure.

You will also develop scalable workflows, guidance, and tools that improve deal turnaround times, documentation quality, and consistency across the region.

This role partners closely with Sales, Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations, with Product and other teams engaged as needed, to resolve deal issues and support accurate execution from quote through contract and booking.

In this role, you will:

 - Serve as the primary Deal Operations contact for AMER account teams, managing deal intake, prioritizing requests, and guiding sellers through pricing, review, and approval processes.

 - Review quotes and proposed commercial terms, including discounts, payment schedules, contract duration, and customer commitments, for accuracy and alignment with pricing guidelines and commercial policies.

 - Build financial analyses and deal models to assess revenue, margin, discount impact, and profitability, and explain the tradeoffs of proposed deal structures to decision-makers.

 - Partner with Sales to structure deals that meet customer needs and OpenAI’s commercial objectives, recommending alternatives when proposed terms fall outside established guidelines.

 - Coordinate deal reviews and required approvals across Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations. Prepare clear recommendations, document decisions, and escalate exceptions to the appropriate stakeholders.

 - Identify risks in non-standard terms and work with Legal and Finance to resolve contractual, billing, and revenue recognition considerations before execution.

 - Maintain complete deal records and approval documentation in CRM, CPQ, and contract management systems, and partner with Revenue Operations to align approved terms, executed agreements, and booking information.

 - Help develop and maintain deal approval policies, escalation paths, pricing guidance, and standardized templates. Improve workflows to reduce bottlenecks while maintaining appropriate controls.

 - Equip sellers with practical guidance and training on deal requirements and approval processes. Apply AI and automation to improve deal intake, knowledge retrieval, and self-service support.

 - Track Deal Desk metrics such as turnaround time, approval bottlenecks, exception trends, and quote accuracy. Use recurring deal patterns to recommend improvements to commercial policies, processes, and tools.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have:

 - 8+ years of experience in Deal Desk, commercial finance, pricing, sales operations, or a related function, preferably in a high-growth technology environment.

 - Hands-on experience reviewing and structuring complex enterprise deals and supporting quoting, commercial approvals, and contracting processes.

 - Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, including experience assessing pricing, discounts, revenue, margins, and deal profitability.

 - Knowledge of enterprise software commercial terms and subscription or consumption-based business models, with the judgment to identify issues that require Legal or Finance review.

 - Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to explain commercial tradeoffs, make clear recommendations, and coordinate timely decisions across teams.

 - Experience with CRM systems, configure-price-quote (CPQ) tools, and contract management platforms, along with strong spreadsheet skills.

 - Attention to detail and a track record of improving approval workflows, documentation, and operational processes as a business scales.

 - Sound commercial judgment and the ability to manage competing priorities and tight deadlines while maintaining accuracy and appropriate controls.

 - A collaborative, hands-on approach to supporting sales teams and familiarity with using AI and automation to improve deal workflows and productivity.

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Growth team drives adoption and revenue for ChatGPT. This role focuses on B2B and small-business growth: helping business owners, functional leaders, and teams discover how ChatGPT can solve their work challenges and deliver value. We partner across product, engineering, product marketing, content, design, and analytics to turn customer insights and disciplined experimentation into sustainable growth.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a growth marketer with deep expertise in search engine optimization (SEO) and a strong experimental approach to answer engine optimization (AEO) to grow ChatGPT adoption among small businesses. You will own the strategy and execution for reaching business buyers through organic search and AI-powered answers, connecting discovery to evaluation, workspace creation, and paid adoption.

You will build an organic acquisition program around how small businesses research problems, compare solutions, and choose tools for their teams. Your remit spans technical SEO, search and question research, content strategy, and AEO experimentation. You will partner with SMB Product Marketing and Content Marketing to translate business use cases, industry needs, and customer proof into useful discovery experiences, and with Web Growth to improve the path from organic discovery to conversion.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA or New York, NY. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own the B2B / SMB SEO and AEO roadmap, prioritizing opportunities by business audience, use case, industry, buying intent, and potential contribution to customer acquisition and revenue.

 - Lead keyword, question, and audience research across the small-business buying journey—from identifying a business problem to comparing solutions and evaluating pricing, team adoption, and business requirements. Translate findings into prioritized content briefs and page opportunities.

 - Own the technical SEO roadmap with web and engineering partners, including crawlability, indexing, rendering, site architecture, internal linking, structured data, and migration readiness. Build durable foundations for discovering and understanding our business content.

 - Develop and test AEO approaches that help business buyers find accurate, useful information about ChatGPT in AI-powered search and answer experiences. Improve answer-focused content, product information, and supporting evidence; track visibility, citations, and referral quality while distinguishing observed results from hypotheses.

 - Partner with SMB Product Marketing and Content Marketing on use-case and industry pages, comparison and evaluation content, practical guides, and customer stories. Bring search insights and clear briefs; maintain accuracy, originality, and usefulness as the program scales.

 - Build measurement with Analytics that connects organic discovery to qualified business traffic, workspace creation, activation, paid conversion, and revenue. Segment performance by intent, audience, and market, and use experiments and cohort analysis to assess impact and attribution limits.

 - Partner with Web Growth, Design, and Product on landing-page and conversion experiments that help business visitors take the right next step. Align messaging, proof points, calls to action, and onward journeys with buyer intent, then evaluate downstream customer quality.

 - Build AI-assisted workflows for research, briefing, content refreshes, technical audits, and reporting, with human review and quality controls. Use programmatic approaches where they create distinct value for business audiences.

 - Coordinate execution across engineering, product marketing, content, web, and analytics partners. Establish a regular testing and learning cadence, and partner on localization to expand proven SEO and AEO approaches into priority markets.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE:

 - 10+ years in SEO or growth marketing, with a track record of growing qualified organic acquisition for B2B software or products serving small businesses. Experience with self-serve or product-led business acquisition is especially relevant.

 - Deep technical SEO expertise, including site architecture, crawling and indexing, structured data, migrations, and internal linking, combined with strong judgment about search intent and content quality.

 - Hands-on experience testing visibility in AI-powered search and answer experiences. You can design an AEO measurement approach, evaluate citations and referrals, and explain what the evidence does—and does not—show.

 - A strong understanding of small-business buyers and how their needs vary by role, company size, and industry. You can turn customer problems, solution comparisons, and buying questions into a focused organic growth strategy.

 - Strong collaboration with product marketing, content, engineering, design, web growth, and analytics teams. You can turn insights into clear briefs, prioritize shared roadmaps, and take initiatives through launch and iteration.

 - Strong analytical and experimentation skills, including search and web analytics, funnel and cohort analysis, and landing-page testing. You connect traffic and visibility to activation, paid adoption, and revenue rather than optimizing for rankings alone.

 - Hands-on experience publishing, refreshing, and measuring content through a CMS, including landing pages, reusable templates, and localized experiences. You are comfortable moving between strategic planning, technical audits, and page-level QA.

 - Experience using AI-assisted workflows and programmatic SEO to improve execution while preserving factual accuracy, original value, and a high-quality customer experience.

 - A test-and-learn mindset, clear communication, and comfort operating in a fast-changing environment. You balance curiosity about new discovery channels with disciplined prioritization and measurement.

The HR Business Partner (HRBP) team at OpenAI partners with leaders on complex organizational and talent decisions where the right path is not always obvious. We stay close enough to the business to understand how it works and focus our time on the decisions that benefit most from our judgment, context, and influence.

We work with urgency, empathy, and sound judgment. We value sincerity, intellectual honesty, and collaboration over ego.


ABOUT THIS ROLE

As a Senior HR Business Partner supporting Tech, you’ll partner with leaders in engineering, product, and other technical teams as they build and scale their organizations. You’ll get close enough to the work to understand what’s slowing teams down, then help leaders make decisions about structure, talent, and how teams work together as technical priorities evolve.

This is an individual contributor role reporting to an HRBP Lead. You’ll advise senior leaders on complex decisions and work directly with managers to make those decisions stick.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Translate technical priorities into org and talent decisions. Help leaders decide what capabilities to build, how to structure teams, and where ownership needs to sit.

 - Diagnose what’s getting in the way of team performance. Use data and input from the people doing the work to separate structural issues from problems with roles, priorities, or how teams work together.

title: Researcher, Frontier Robustness
description:
About the Team

The Frontier Robustness team advances the science of securing frontier AI systems. We develop new methods to keep increasingly capable models contained, observable, and under human control, focusing on the sandboxes, shared research infrastructure, and protective systems used during model development and evaluation.

We use our most capable models to discover and combine weaknesses across the security stack, studying how they might escape containment, communicate through unauthorized channels, or evade monitoring. We turn these findings into new defenses and test whether protections hold as models, environments, and attack strategies change.



About the Role

We are looking for a researcher to develop and test new methods for securing frontier AI systems. You will investigate open-ended questions about model behavior, containment, and safeguards—designing experiments, building evaluations, and developing defenses where established approaches may be insufficient. You will work closely with the Security organization to define the problems and translate research findings into practical protections.

You will take research from an initial question and threat model through experiment design, reproducible findings, and tested defenses. You will write code, build tools and prototypes, and work closely with researchers and infrastructure owners to turn new ideas into safeguards that work in practice. This requires sound security judgment, comfort with uncertainty, and the ability to devise solutions to problems without established answers. This role is based in San Francisco.



In this role, you will:

 - Design and run experiments using frontier models and hands-on security techniques to discover failure modes in sandboxes, research infrastructure, and the services models can reach. Reproduce vulnerabilities and assess their impact.

 - Develop threat models and novel adversarial tests for attacks that cross multiple security boundaries, including sandbox escapes, unauthorized communication between agents, and access to sensitive data or systems through shared services.

 - Invent, prototype, and evaluate defenses that strengthen isolation and limit the impact of a compromised boundary. Study agent permissions and tool configurations to identify excessive access and build layered protections with infrastructure owners.

 - Develop and red-team model-based safeguards and monitors of model reasoning and actions. Investigate evasion, test new monitoring techniques, and measure when protections detect or prevent unsafe behavior.

 - Develop automated adversarial tests and repeatable evaluations to measure progress as model capabilities, configurations, and attack strategies change. Assess whether defenses generalize to new attacks, verify fixes, and identify regressions.

 - Partner across Research, Security, and infrastructure teams, including Agent Security, to prioritize risks and turn findings into deployed improvements while accounting for performance and researcher workflows.
   
   

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have hands-on experience conducting research with large language models, including designing and running experiments and evaluating model behavior.

 - Can turn an open-ended question into a clear hypothesis, build reproducible experiments at scale, and use the results to develop or improve a method.

 - Can design rigorous evaluations, investigate unexpected results, and test whether findings hold across different models, environments, and attack strategies.

 - Write and debug code independently, build research tools and prototypes, and carry ideas through experimentation.

 - Bring practical security experience relevant to this work, such as sandboxing, vulnerability research, adversarial testing, or detection and monitoring.

 - Work effectively with Security and infrastructure partners to develop threat models, interpret findings, and turn promising research into deployed safeguards.

 - Experience with operating systems, containers or virtualization, distributed infrastructure, or AI agents would also be valuable.

title: Software Engineer, Presence
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Presence is OpenAI’s team building AI agents that organizations can trust to handle real conversations and get things done. Our mission is to turn advances in frontier models into dependable systems that can resolve customer issues, support employees, and improve through experience in production.

Imagine calling about an unexpected charge. An agent needs to understand your situation, verify your identity, find the relevant account information, apply the right policy, and resolve the issue or bring in a person. It needs to do all of this naturally, accurately, and quickly, even when the conversation takes an unexpected turn. Presence brings together the models, execution systems, integrations, and controls that make experiences like this possible across voice, chat and email.

One of our most exciting challenges is what happens after an agent goes live. We're building a system for understanding where agents fail and making them better: investigate a production conversation, reproduce the problem in an evaluation, use Codex to develop a fix, test it against the current agent, and measure the result after deployment. Our ambition is to make more of this improvement process agentic over time, while giving people control over what changes reach users.

Read the launch announcement https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/.

 


WHAT WE WORK ON

 - Realtime voice: Natural conversations with fast responses, interruptions, and reliable audio, even under heavy traffic.

 - Agent systems: Orchestration, reasoning, tool execution, integrations with company systems, and enforcing permissions and policies.

 - Agent quality: Production debugging, simulations, evaluation infrastructure, regression testing, and measuring whether changes improve real outcomes.

 - Product and developer experience: Making it easier for teams to build, test, deploy, and operate sophisticated agents using Codex and OpenAI's capabilities.

 


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

You'll work at the intersection of frontier research, product engineering, and production systems, with a direct feedback loop from people using what you build. We collaborate closely with Research, Forward Deployed Engineers, and customers to understand where models and systems break down and turn those lessons into improvements that can benefit many deployments.

The impact is already tangible. At launch, Presence was resolving 75% of issues coming into OpenAI's English phone support without a human, and its Codex-assisted improvement process helped cut transfers to people by 15 percentage points over ten days. Introducing OpenAI Presence https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/

We're looking for people excited by ambitious engineering problems, building products people depend on, and helping define how AI agents are developed and improved in the real world.

 - 9+ years of professional engineering experience, excluding internships, in backend, platform, or product engineering roles.

 - A track record of hands-on technical leadership, including setting architecture, breaking complex problems into clear implementation plans, and guiding engineers through delivery.

 - Deep backend engineering and systems design skills, with proficiency in at least one backend programming language and experience designing services, data models, and interfaces that remain reliable as usage grows.

 - End-to-end ownership of complex systems or product capabilities, from ambiguous requirements and technical design through implementation, launch, and production iteration.

 - Strong production engineering judgment: you can diagnose difficult failures, reason about performance and scalability, and improve reliability through testing, observability, and operational discipline.

 - Strong product judgment that connects technical decisions to user needs, with the ability to balance delivery speed, reliability, security, and long-term maintainability.

description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.
Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.
We are looking for a Senior Data Analyst — Hardware to join our Data Analytics team in North America. You will be the analytics lead on the data that measures the success and quality of ŌURA's hardware portfolio—how rings perform, sell, activate, and hold up for our members over their lifecycle.This is the data behind hardware portfolio performance—revenue, units sold, sell-through, activation, COGS, margin—and the quality signals, including warranty, RMA/returns, and defect rates, that show up in board and public reporting. This role will ensure that ŌURA continues to be a scalable consumer-hardware business while migrating to a unified data platform on Databricks. You will make sure the numbers that leadership and external auditors steer by—units sold, sell-through, activation rate, warranty rate, and defect/quality rate—are defined once, computed correctly, are traceable end-to-end from source systems to the executive dashboard, and audit-ready. You will partner with Hardware Engineering, Quality, Product, Finance, and Data Engineering to build the governed hardware data foundation.
What You Will Do:
Hardware KPI Ownership
Own the analytics layer for the hardware portfolio scorecard—partner with Hardware Engineering, Product, Quality, and Finance to define, document, and deliver the KPIs that show up in board and external reporting (including but not limited to activation rate, warranty rate, return/RMA rate, and defect/quality rate).
Establish each hardware KPI as a governed, audit-grade data product—locked definitions, single owner, data build tool (dbt) tests, full lineage from source systems, formal sign-off, and a documented change-management process.
Build and own the hardware data products.
Be the analytics representative in external audit cycles—produce documentation, walk auditors through lineage, and ensure controls and traceability are reflected in how hardware portfolio and quality metrics are produced.
Hardware Quality & Portfolio Performance Analytics
Partner closely with Hardware Engineering and Firmware teams on product quality data—defect rates, failure modes, warranty claims, RMA root cause, and field reliability by product generation, SKU, and manufacturing batch.
Deliver hardware portfolio performance analytics—sell-through, activation, and retention by product generation and SKU—that give Hardware leadership a single trusted view of what's working and what isn't.
Drive adoption of self-service reporting by Hardware Engineering, Quality, and Product partners using a variety of analytics tools and creating clear documentation to reduce one-off reporting and free up analyst time for analysis.
Platform Migration & Data Engineering
Migrate hardware portfolio and quality reporting from legacy stacks (Snowflake + Tableau + Sheets) to our Databricks-based platform, with dbt-modeled metrics, Unity Catalog lineage, and Databricks SQL / Genie as the executive-facing surface.
Coordinate with source-system owners across manufacturing, quality systems, and e-commerce (NetSuite, contract-manufacturer feeds, Zuora) and the Data Engineering team to ensure clean ingestion, correct dimensional modeling, and clear lineage from factory output through to sell-through, activation, and quality events.
Resolve systems data quality issues to ensure that reporting is trustworthy end to end.
Build and maintain the Hardware domain's data products in Databricks, mentoring analysts on dimensional modeling, dbt practices, and the Golden Path for publishing governed metrics for reporting and for MCP/agentic AI consumption.
Tooling & Innovation
Continuously evaluate emerging tools (Unity Catalog, Databricks Genie, AI-assisted SQL/modeling via Cursor and Claude Code, semantic-layer technologies) to improve productivity and accuracy in hardware portfolio and quality reporting.
We have offices in San Francisco, San Diego and Los Angeles for those who prefer hybrid or office settings. ŌURA employees in other major cities (like Boston and New York) occasionally gather informally at local co-working locations.
What you'll bring:
7+ years in analytics, business intelligence, or a related data-focused role, with at least 3+ years specifically supporting Hardware, Product Quality, or Manufacturing.
Demonstrated experience building executive-level reporting for a physical-product business that is trusted by leadership and survives external scrutiny (Board, auditors, investors).
Deep working knowledge of hardware data domains: BOM and component costing, warranty and RMA/returns, defect and quality rates, manufacturing yield, and how transactional systems (ERP, contract-manufacturer feeds, hardware use platforms) flow into reported numbers.
Expert in SQL with experience writing complex queries for operational and financial data extraction, reconciliation, and modeling.
Expertise in dimensional modeling for hardware and quality reporting (conformed dimensions across SKU, product generation, channel, geo; slowly-changing dimensions for product and cost hierarchies; period-over-period comparisons).
Experience with dbt—including tests, documentation, exposures, and contracts.
Experience with Databricks strongly preferred (Unity Catalog, Databricks SQL, Lakeflow, Genie); deep Snowflake experience acceptable with willingness to migrate.
Experience with modern BI tools (Tableau, Looker, Databricks SQL Dashboards, Power BI) and a clear point of view on when each is the right fit.
Track record of working alongside external auditors (PwC, Deloitte, EY, KPMG) and building documentation that withstands audit review.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills—able to brief a hardware or finance leader on a number, then explain to an analyst how the data behind it works.
Thrive in a fast-paced, highly collaborative global work environment that spans engineering, quality, and offices across time zones.
Nice to have:
What Makes You Stand Out • Familiarity with adjacent tooling and sources: AWS, GitHub, NetSuite/ERP, Fivetran, Python, semantic layers, quality management systems (QMS), and contract-manufacturer (CM) data integrations.
Experience standing up a hardware data contract and product/SKU dimension (dim_hardware) from scratch in a high-growth consumer hardware company.
Experience building governed KPI programs through a formal external audit (e.g., PwC, Big 4), including COGS, quality, and units-sold reconciliation.
Expertise in data visualization theory—you understand how to choose the right chart for the right message and why exec dashboards fail when they don't.

Everpure (NYSE: P) has evolved from storage pioneer to data platform, closing fiscal 2026 with $3.7 billion in revenue, its first billion-dollar quarter, and accelerating growth into FY27. Our strategic agenda spans the companies defining the next era of technology - hyperscalers, AI labs, the AI hardware supply chain, data platform providers, and the broader AI ecosystem.
This type of work—work that changes the world—is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us.
THE ROLE
We are seeking an experienced Platform Software Engineer for our Systems Software Team. You will be working as part of a dynamic team and will be responsible for designing, developing, and testing system software functionality for Pure’s upcoming platforms. The work spans the gamut of Systems software and you will have the opportunity to work in a wide range of areas and features ranging from Platform drivers to networking and storage layers.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Plan and influence the lifecycle of new Hardware Platforms.  Work on problems ranging from design, bring up, to deployment, upgrades and fleet level reliability.
Participate in the full lifecycle of new hardware platforms from early bring up through manufacturing release.  Work closely with peer teams to debug complex HW/FW of new server hardware, including CPUs, chipsets, and peripheral components. Debug complex HW/FW issues across x86, PCIe, NVMe, and networking using lab tools (oscilloscope, logic analyzer, JTAG) and kernel/driver traces.
Design, implement and improve remote server management capabilities (e.g., using standards like Redfish) and enhance Reliability, Availability, and Serviceability (RAS) features.
Design, write and maintain software components in C/C++, Python, Golang and RUST.
Collaborate with vendors on requirements specification and follow through to system delivery.
Work closely with hardware engineers, system architects, and operating system developers to define specifications, review designs, and ensure seamless hardware-software integration.
REQUIREMENTS:
Preferred B.S or M.S in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Proficiency in C/C++ (object oriented design and C++ 11 and onwards) and strong Python skills for build/test automation and lab tooling. Experience in Golang and RUST is desirable.
Strong interest in CPU Architecture and Data Centre Hardware. Desire to dive deep in solving problems at the intersection of hardware and software.
Experience leading teams and projects both within the organization and across cross-functional groups.
Hands on experience with hardware platforms, including design/requirements feedback, bring-up, system-level debugging, customer delivery, and support.
Experience with most or all of: CPU architectures, BMC, BIOS, PCI-e, I2C (and SMBUS, PMBUS variants).
Solid Linux skills (kernel logs, drivers, bootloaders) and ability to root‑cause across HW/FW/OS boundaries.
Good verbal communication & collaboration skills.
NICE TO HAVE REQUIREMENTS
Prior experience shipping /supporting enterprise class x86 based appliances
Prior experience with BMC firmware, OpenBMC or equivalent, and management protocols such as Redfish/IPMI.
Prior experience with BIOS/UEFI development and/or debugging
#LI-ONSITE
Salary ranges are determined based on role, level and location. For positions open to candidates in multiple geographical locations, the base salary range is reflective of the labor market across the applicable locations.
This role may be eligible for incentive pay and/or equity.
There is no application deadline and we accept applications on an ongoing basis until the job is filled.
The annual base salary range is: $180,000 — $270,000 USD WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT FROM US:
Innovation : We celebrate those who think critically, like a challenge, and aspire to be trailblazers.
Growth : We give you the space and support to grow along with us and to contribute to something meaningful. We have been named Fortune's Best Workplaces in Technology™, Fortune's Best Workplaces in the Bay Area™, and certified as a Great Place to Work®!
Team : We build each other up and set aside ego for the greater good.
And because we understand the value of bringing your full and best self to work, we offer a variety of perks to manage a healthy balance, including flexible time off, wellness resources, and company-sponsored team events. Check out http://benefits.everpuredata.com/ for more information.
ACCOMMODATIONS AND ACCESSIBILITY:
Candidates with disabilities may request accommodations for all aspects of our hiring process. For more on this, contact us at TA-Ops@purestorage.com if you’re invited to an interview.
OUR COMMITMENT TO A STRONG AND INCLUSIVE TEAM:
We’re forging a future where everyone finds their rightful place and where every voice matters. Where uniqueness isn’t just accepted but embraced. That’s why we are committed to fostering the growth and development of every person, cultivating a sense of community through our Employee Resource Groups and advocating for inclusive leadership.

title: Director of Facilities
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Director of Facilities
The Director of Facilities will have end-to-end accountability for the operational performance, physical condition, safety, functionality, and employee experience of Quince's headquarters in both San Francisco and Palo Alto.  This is a hands-on role that will require on-location presence in both locations weekly.
A defining responsibility of this position will be helping Quince transition into a significantly larger, more complex headquarters building in San Francisco. The Director will partner with internal leadership, the relocation project manager, architects, contractors, and service providers to ensure the new headquarters is fully operational, exceptionally maintained, and equipped to support the company's continued growth.  The role will
Following the relocation, this leader will oversee all aspects of headquarters facilities operations, including building systems, maintenance, workplace services, security coordination, vendor management, budgets, sample and fabric library operations, and ongoing improvements.
The Director will also lead a team of Sample and Fabric Library Coordinators, ensuring product samples and fabric materials are accurately tracked, organized, maintained, and readily accessible to Quince's merchandising, product development, design, and other internal teams.
Responsibilities
1. New Headquarters Relocation & Operational Readiness
Play a central leadership role in Quince's relocation to a substantially larger and more comprehensive headquarters in San Francisco.
Partner with the relocation project manager, architects, construction teams, designers, IT, Security, and executive leadership to ensure a successful transition.
Develop and execute a comprehensive facilities operational-readiness plan for the new headquarters.
Oversee building systems commissioning, operational testing, inspections, and facilities handover.
Establish required maintenance programs, vendor contracts, workplace services, and operating procedures prior to occupancy.
Ensure the new headquarters supports a significantly larger employee population and more complex workplace services.
Coordinate the readiness of conference facilities, employee amenities, shared spaces, and sample and fabric library areas.
Develop staffing plans, operating budgets, and service standards appropriate for the new facility.
Lead post-occupancy stabilization and establish a scalable facilities operating model.
2. Headquarters Operations & Maintenance
Own day-to-day facilities operations, ensuring a safe, clean, functional, and professionally maintained workplace.
Oversee HVAC, electrical, plumbing, lighting, elevators, building management systems, and other critical infrastructure.
Develop preventive and predictive maintenance programs to maximize reliability and minimize disruptions.
Manage janitorial services, repairs, waste management, pest control, and general building maintenance.
Establish a centralized work-order management system with defined service-level expectations.
Ensure facilities issues are resolved with urgency and accountability.
3. Workplace Experience & Employee Services
Create and maintain a headquarters environment that reflects Quince's brand, culture, and commitment to excellence.
Oversee conference rooms, meeting facilities, kitchens, breakrooms, common areas, and employee amenities.
Manage food, beverage, coffee, snack, and related workplace service programs as applicable.
Partner with IT to ensure meeting spaces and audiovisual systems remain functional.
Support company meetings, leadership events, and headquarters activities.
Continuously improve employee workplace experience through responsive service and thoughtful facilities management.
4. Sample & Fabric Library Management
Directly manage and develop a team of Sample and Fabric Library Coordinators responsible for the organization, tracking, storage, and movement of product samples and fabric materials.
Establish and enforce standardized procedures for sample intake, labeling, cataloging, storage, checkout, transfers, and disposition.
Maintain highly accurate sample and fabric inventories, ensuring materials are properly identified, recorded, and readily accessible.
Implement inventory control systems and periodic physical audits to maintain sample inventory accuracy above 95% .
Partner with Merchandising, Design, Product Development, and other stakeholders to ensure samples and fabrics are available when needed.
Establish clear accountability for missing, misplaced, damaged, or incorrectly cataloged samples.
Optimize library layouts, storage capacity, organization, and retrieval processes within the new headquarters.
Oversee the relocation and accurate reconciliation of existing sample and fabric inventories into the new facility.
Develop KPIs and reporting for sample accuracy, retrieval efficiency, inventory discrepancies, and library service levels.
Continuously improve sample handling processes to reduce loss, improve accessibility, and increase operational efficiency.
5. Financial Management & Cost Optimization
Develop and manage annual headquarters facilities operating budgets and capital expenditure plans.
Establish financial models and operating budgets for the larger headquarters facility.
Maintain financial controls over utilities, maintenance, contracted services, workplace amenities, and capital projects.
Identify cost efficiencies without compromising workplace quality or operational reliability.
Negotiate competitive vendor agreements and monitor performance.
Develop multiyear capital maintenance and infrastructure replacement plans.
Provide regular financial reporting, forecasts, and variance analyses.
6. Vendor & Contract Management
Select, negotiate, and manage third-party facilities service providers.
Establish measurable service-level agreements and performance expectations.
Conduct vendor performance reviews and implement corrective actions when necessary.
Ensure contractors comply with safety, insurance, regulatory, and company requirements.
Maintain productive relationships with landlords, property management, building engineers, and service providers.
7. Safety, Security & Regulatory Compliance
Ensure compliance with applicable building, fire, life-safety, accessibility, environmental, and workplace regulations.
Partner with Security, People, Legal, and IT to maintain physical security and workplace safety programs.
Oversee emergency preparedness, evacuation procedures, and facilities-related business continuity planning.
Coordinate required inspections, permits, certifications, and regulatory documentation.
Proactively identify and mitigate facilities-related operational and safety risks.
8. Space Planning & Facilities Strategy
Partner with leadership to anticipate future space requirements and organizational growth.
Optimize workstations, conference rooms, shared spaces, employee amenities, and sample and fabric library storage.
Coordinate office reconfigurations, furniture installations, and internal moves.
Establish systems to track space utilization, facilities assets, and capital investments.
Develop a multiyear facilities strategy balancing employee experience, operating costs, capacity, and infrastructure reliability.
9. Team Leadership & Operational Excellence
Build and lead a high-performing facilities organization appropriate for the scale and complexity of the new headquarters.
Directly manage the Sample and Fabric Library Coordinators, establishing clear responsibilities, productivity expectations, inventory accuracy standards, and development plans.
Establish operating procedures, performance expectations, and escalation protocols across facilities and library operations.
Implement technology for maintenance management, asset tracking, sample inventory management, vendor oversight, and reporting.
Create a culture of urgency, accountability, service excellence, and continuous improvement.
Establish measurable KPIs and regularly report performance to leadership.
Qualifications
Required
Bachelor's degree in Facilities Management, Engineering, Construction Management, Business Administration, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
10+ years of progressive facilities management or corporate real estate operations experience.
5+ years of leadership experience managing large, complex corporate office environments.
Demonstrated experience operating a major corporate headquarters or similarly sophisticated commercial facility.
Direct experience supporting a major headquarters relocation, new building opening, or large-scale office transition.
Strong understanding of commercial building systems, preventive maintenance, workplace services, and life-safety requirements.
Experience developing and managing significant operating budgets and capital expenditures.
Proven success managing complex vendor relationships and service contracts.
Experience leading operational teams with measurable service and inventory accuracy expectations.
Strong project management, organizational, and problem-solving capabilities.
Ability to operate effectively in a rapidly growing organization.
Exceptional attention to detail, responsiveness, and commitment to operational excellence.
Preferred

title: Head of Data Science
description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
Samsara's Data Science, ML, and Data Platform team brings together data science, production ML, data engineering, and data platform to turn emerging AI capabilities into reliable products. These products help customers run safer, more efficient physical operations. As Head of Data Science, ML, and Data Platform, you will lead about 30 people through experienced managers and senior technical leaders, and report to the SVP of Engineering. You will decide where agents, foundation models, classical ML, and statistical methods belong at Samsara, and you will turn what you learn into how the whole organization works.
In this role, you will:
Define an AI-native strategy and rethink the roadmap from first principles as capabilities change. Choose what to build, buy, stop, and scale.
Partner with Product and Engineering to take intelligence from experiment to deployment, adoption, and continuous improvement in customer experiences.
Build a trusted data foundation by making certified metrics, discoverable metadata, and traceable outputs available to people and agents across the organization, within clear permissions.
Own production and economic outcomes, including reliability, latency, inference and infrastructure cost, and human oversight. Make evaluation a core capability, with failure modes, uncertainty, and regressions visible during development.
Build a leadership team of managers and senior individual contributors and develop them. Hire people who combine scientific rigor, engineering ability, and a drive to keep learning.

About Samsara Hardware Engineering:
Samsara's hardware systems bridge the gap between the rapidly evolving world of physical operations and our cloud platform that enables our customers to increase the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of their operations which power the global economy. The hardware footprint is big – we build ultra-low power sensors, ruggedized asset trackers, vehicle ADAS systems with AI/ML, telematics systems, and rackmount video inspection with AI/ML, with more to come in the future. We leverage myriad technologies including injection molding, sheet metal, precision optics, gaskets and seals, thermal materials, adhesives, and more. Our challenges range from ingress sealing, thermal management, structural analysis, and drop and vibration survival to material selection, design for manufacturability, tooling optimization, and cost reduction, all in products built to survive extreme environments.
About the role:
We're looking for a Product Design (Mechanical Engineering) co-op to join our team. In the day-to-day, you will be responsible for working on the mechanical aspects of the design of products based on thorough feasibility, design, and cost studies encompassing enclosure architecture, materials selection, thermal management, sealing, etc. We have a tremendous amount of telemetry and access to customers that help guide our design process. You will work directly with our customers to ensure we lead the industry with our product design. We run a collaborative process working closely with Product Management, EE, FW, EPM, NPI, and Hardware leadership to make excellent tradeoffs and choices. Throughout this process, you'll share your expertise with other engineers. The US and Taiwan PD teams are supported by the Supply Chain team, laboratories, JDM design resources, and a growing supply base. You will work closely with these internal and external partners to achieve our objectives.
This role will be held at our San Francisco office. Co-ops are required to be in the office Tuesdays to Thursdays and remote work days on Mondays and Fridays. As part of the co-op program, we do provide relocation and housing support for the duration of the co-op. To be eligible for this role, you must be attending a university that supports full-time work as part of a 6-month co-op OR attend a university that will allow you to take 2 quarters or one semester off to work a co-op. Please do not apply if you are unable to commit to the full duration of this co-op. We are looking for this co-op to join us from January - June 2027. At this time, we are not accepting first-year co-op students. Ideally, this student is in their junior year of school as an undergraduate student and has previous internship and/or co-op experience.

You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

Contribute to shipping successful product lines.
Conduct research: Stay informed of the latest materials, manufacturing processes, and mechanical technologies from top suppliers and manufacturing partners.

Prototype: Build proof-of-concept models using 3D printing, CNC machining, or quick-turn fabrication for evaluating concepts or jump-starting product development.
Design: Take a concept from industrial design intent through detailed CAD, part and assembly design, and production drawings, spanning enclosures, wiring harnesses and cable assemblies, and product packaging; either on your own or navigate the process with JDM resources.
Test: Create a validation plan for each phase of the product development through PVT and characterize the full mechanical system for ingress protection, drop, shock, vibration, thermal, and environmental performance.
Get hands-on: Install, evaluate, and troubleshoot our products on real vehicles and industrial equipment to understand mounting, cable routing, and real-world use conditions.
Failure analysis: Find the root cause of design inefficiencies and field failures, and improve design to meet performance and quality requirements.
Manage: We bolster our internal development team with top JDM companies to design, validate, certify and manufacture quality products, tooling vendors, certification labs and other external consultants.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.
An ideal candidate has:
Bachelor's degree in progress in Mechanical Engineering or a related technical field. We are looking for second or third-time co-op or Master level co-op students. We will not be considering first-time co-ops. Your target graduation timeline is May-June 2028.
You must be able to commit to a minimum of 6 months of full-time co-op employment and have a university that supports the co-op experience.
Prior intern or co-op experience working on high-volume hardware programs.
Solid fundamentals in mechanical design, materials, mechanics of materials, and thermal management.
CAD part, assembly, and drawing knowledge in Siemens NX, including GD&T and tolerance analysis.
Ability to navigate tradeoffs between design, manufacturability, schedule, and cost.
Hands-on experience with prototyping and test equipment such as 3D printers, machine shop tools, environmental chambers, and drop/vibration test fixtures, and comfort working directly on vehicles and industrial equipment.
Knowledge of injection molding, sheet metal, gaskets and seals for IP-rated enclosures, adhesives, fasteners, wiring harnesses and cable assemblies, and product packaging.
Familiarity with cross-functional EE topics such as PCBAs, antennas, batteries, and connectors is a plus.
Strong ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams and drive independent work.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

Assign EPMs to programs based on complexity and risk, rebalance as the portfolio shifts, and step in personally to drive the most complex or highest-risk program when needed.
Build the recruiting pipeline, interview loop, and onboarding plan that let the team scale without lowering the bar.
Own the hardware launch system
Own the end-to-end hardware development process from investigation and concept through EVT, DVT, PVT, and GA, and tailor it per program so small programs stay light and large programs stay controlled.
Run the OK2 gate reviews (OK2Concept through OK2FCS) with the VP of Hardware Engineering and Hardware Product Management, and hold the organization to the entry and exit criteria for each gate.
Own the integrated program schedule across HW, FW, SW, reliability, compliance, and supply chain, including the xVT build plan, build allocations, and JDM deliverables through PVT.
Set the standard for program status, risk, and decision communication to executives, and run the weekly hardware project review and steering forums.

Manage JDM and CM partner engagement across the development phases, from RFQ through PVT handoff to Operations Program Management.
Partner with Product Management, Supply Chain, Operations, Quality, Compliance, and Finance so that program goals, business cases, and launch commitments stay aligned as programs evolve.
Identify ways to shorten time to market, improve first-pass build yields, and reduce development cost, and drive those improvements across the portfolio rather than one program at a time.

Use AI tools daily to synthesize program data across Slack, Jira, Confluence, Smartsheet, and meeting transcripts; to draft status, risk, and decision documents; and to analyze schedule, cost, and quality data. Validate AI output critically before it reaches stakeholders. You own the result, not the model.
Own adoption and results of AI tooling across the EPM discipline, including the hardware EPM agent that drafts meeting notes, action items, status reports, Confluence updates, and schedule changes for EPM review. Own its roadmap and extend it into risk detection, schedule analysis, and build readiness.
Design, deploy, and iterate AI agents, skills, and automations that remove manual coordination work from program management. Treat AI as a productivity lever before headcount, quantify the hours removed, and reinvest that time into risk management and technical depth.
Set the baseline AI fluency expectation for every EPM on the team, coach to it, and include it in performance and development conversations. Share patterns, prompts, and agent designs across Hardware Engineering and the wider R&D program management community.
Report AI adoption and outcomes (usage, hours saved, cycle-time or quality improvements) to Hardware Engineering leadership on a regular cadence.

Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's Operating Principles as we scale globally and across new offices.

12+ years of experience shipping high-volume hardware programs at scale with ODM and JDM partners overseas, taking products from concept through mass production.
4+ years of experience managing and developing engineering program managers, including hiring, performance management, and coaching across levels.
Proven ownership of a hardware product development process (phase gates, xVT builds, design reviews, PVT handoff) and the judgment to standardize it where it helps and tailor it where it does not.
Strong engineering background with the ability to understand and challenge trade-offs across electrical, mechanical, firmware, reliability, manufacturability, schedule, and cost.
Demonstrated hands-on use of AI tools in your own program management work, and at least one example of an AI workflow, agent, or automation you designed and deployed for a team.
Executive communication skills: concise written and verbal status, risk, and decision communication to VP and C-level stakeholders.
Expertise with program planning tools (Smartsheet or Microsoft Project), Jira and Confluence, and PLM systems for BOM and ECO management.
Ability to travel internationally up to 25% of the time.
BS in a relevant technical field such as EE, ME, or CS, or equivalent experience.
An ideal candidate also has
Worked as an EE, ME, or firmware individual contributor on hardware programs before moving into program management.
Shipped dash cameras, telematics gateways, asset trackers, or other ruggedized, cellular-connected IoT devices with embedded AI/ML.
Built or led an AI agent, Cursor skill, or automation program adopted by a team beyond your own, with measured results.
Led distributed teams across the US and Taiwan or China, and worked directly with Taiwan-based JDM design centers and factories.
Experience bringing firmware and hardware development onto a single integrated schedule, including OTA readiness at launch.
MS in a technical field or an MBA.

description:

title: Senior Quality Inspector (Mechanical)
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots builds AI-native industrial robot arms deployed at manufacturing facilities across the U.S. In June 2026 we closed a $200M Series C at a $1B valuation, led by RoboStrategy with continued backing from General Catalyst and new participation from the Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund and Samsung Next.


About the role

Robots only work if every part is exactly what it claims to be — and that's on you. You'll be the final word on mechanical quality in the QC lab, using GD&T to catch what others miss, leading first article inspections, and making sure the parts going into our robots actually match the drawings they came from.


What you'll do

- Perform GD&T inspection (ASME Y14.5) on mechanical parts and assemblies in the QC lab, catching deviations before they become problems downstream

- Program and operate CMMs and other advanced measurement equipment to verify parts against spec

- Lead First Article Inspections for mechanical parts at launch and after any process change

- Run process audits on production mechanical operations to keep quality consistent at scale

- Mentor Receiving Inspectors on mechanical inspection techniques and GD&T fundamentals

- Keep inspection records and traceability tight and audit-ready for all mechanical work

- Sit on the Material Review Board to help resolve mechanical nonconformances

- Review mechanical drawings for inspectability, flagging GD&T issues to NPI and Engineering before they cause rework

- Support 6S and FOD programs to keep the QC lab area clean, organized, and safe


What you'll bring

- 5+ years of mechanical inspection experience in a QC lab environment

- Strong working knowledge of GD&T per ASME Y14.5

- Hands-on proficiency with measurement equipment — CMM preferred, plus height gauges, optical comparators, and surface plates

- Sharp drawing interpretation skills

- The patience and precision to work through complex measurement tasks without cutting corners


Nice to have

- CMM programming experience with PC-DMIS, Calypso, or similar software

- Experience inspecting industrial robotics or precision mechanical assemblies

The Platform Velocity Sales team works with B2B Software Platforms to help them facilitate payments for their customers using our Stripe Connect product.
